# Edge Program — Per-Story Prompts (standalone sessions)

**What this is:** one **`▶ Story prompt`** per *not-yet-completed* story across every epic, so any Trello card can be pulled and run in a fresh Claude Code session on its own (per the guide §0.4 convention). Companion to `edge_program_implementation_guide.md` (the stories' full tasks/AC live there) + `edge_program_technical_spec.md` (design) + `sport_data_platform.md`.
**Last updated:** 2026-06-18 _(refresh on any material change)_

🚨 **GLOBAL RUN-COMMAND CONVENTION (operator 2026-07-02 — applies to EVERY prompt/session, incl. mid-session):** whenever you tell the operator to RUN something, ALWAYS give (a) **WHERE — laptop or the EC2 box** (box commands must be the full `docker compose … exec … python scripts/X.py …` wrapper, `-e AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2` for DuckDB-S3; see `services/dagster/aws/BOX_OPERATIONS.md`) and (b) the **FULL copy-pasteable command** (exact flags/paths/env — no prose "run the X script", no unfilled placeholders). The operator loses time chasing this otherwise.

🧭 **MODEL-TIER RUBRIC (operator 2026-08-03 — how to assign the `🧭` tag; applies program-wide, both catalogs):**
- **🧭 SONNET** — lowest cost; SIMPLE, low-complexity tasks that do NOT touch critical infrastructure (serving path, pipeline/Dagster ops, model promotion/registry, prod data writes). App display, docs, config, straightforward CRUD/UX over ALREADY-SHIPPED machinery.
- **🧭 OPUS** — the DEFAULT for anything COMPLEX **or** touching critical infrastructure: serving/pipeline changes, incidents, §0.5 modeling, cross-cutting reconciliation, and anything CI can't validate (the runtime-gate class). "Everything Sonnet can't do."
- **🧭 FABLE** — the deepest dives; the MOST expensive → use SPARINGLY, reserved for the MOST complex, HIGH-VALUE **MODELING** work (the hardest bake-offs/optimizations, e.g. E11.31). ⛔ never a default; the spend must be justified.
- ⇒ ⛔ retire loose dual-tags like "SONNET/FABLE" — pick ONE deliberately. When a mostly-simple story has one infra-touching slice, either scope that slice out or tag the whole story OPUS.

🌿 **WORKTREE-PROMPT CONVENTION (2026-08-03): the OPERATOR names the branch when pre-creating the worktree, so a prompt's suggested branch name is only a DEFAULT** (used if a session creates its own worktree). ⛔ when writing the pre-created-worktree confirm-check, do NOT pin a SPECIFIC name ("must print `<name>`") — write "confirm `git branch --show-current` is a DEDICATED story branch, NOT `dev`/`main`; the exact name is whatever the operator created." (The doc-fix workflow test hit this: prompt suggested `docfix-aws-resources-lambda`, the worktree was `aws-resources-fix` → a FALSE mismatch the session correctly flagged. Pinning a name manufactures a false alarm; the real invariant is "not dev/main.")
- 🌿 **READINESS-CHECK OUTPUT (2026-08-03): every prompt readiness check ENDS with the WORKTREE NAME + the copy-pasteable create command** — `git worktree add ../<slug> -b <slug> dev && cp .env ../<slug>/.env` then `code ../<slug>` — where `<slug>` is a story-descriptive lowercase-hyphenated name (DIR = BRANCH, identical). The operator no longer invents a name; PM supplies it in the check.
🕐 **TIME-REPORTING CONVENTION (operator 2026-08-04): any time reported TO THE OPERATOR — in PM chat, a card, a scheduled-run instruction, a handoff — is in CST (Central), NOT UTC.** Convert to Central before presenting (Aug = the operator's Central wall clock, UTC−5). UTC stays fine INSIDE technical artifacts where it's load-bearing (`account_usage` timestamps, `game_date` UTC buckets, cron UTC, midnight-UTC-straddle logic) — but the operator-facing "when to run / when it happened" is CST. A prompt that reports a time back to the operator does the same.

**How to use:** copy a story's block into a fresh session. Blocks are **compact by design** — they inherit shared context by reference (§ = sections of the implementation guide). Every block assumes the **§0.1 conventions**: `dbtf` (not `dbt`); Snowflake via the Snowflake MCP, fully-qualified, no `USE`; never a live Snowflake query on a request path; `uv run python`; hand >1-min scripts to the operator; **do not git commit/push**; market-blind for non-market models (Principle 3); honest-framing for anything user-facing (no win-rate/edge claims). **CI gates BEFORE handoff (never hand off red code): Python → `uv run pytest` (Unit Tests CI); dbt → `dbtf build --select state:modified+` AND `dbtf compile` (both dbt-Build CI jobs) — all green first.** **Every session (model track included) ENDS with an `⏭️ Operator handoff`: the CI-gate result + run-order commands + a copy-pasteable `git add <paths>` of every changed/created file to commit (code, dbt, `sub_model_registry.yaml`, `ablation_results/*.md`, doc edits) + what NOT to commit (artifacts → S3/registry) — so the repo never drifts out of sync.**

**App stories — one fresh session per story:** run app work **one story at a time, each in its own clean session.** For any **[App]** story: open a fresh session, paste the **application-session bootstrap prompt** (persisted at **`app_session_bootstrap.md`**), then paste **exactly one** story block — build, then **end with the `⏭️ Operator handoff` checklist** (Lambda rebuild/deploy, dbt commands, scripts to run, the `git add` for files to deploy, changelog line, verify-after-deploy) so the operator knows exactly what to run. Do **not** chain multiple stories through one long-lived session. App surfaces marked **⏳ §0.3** are **not hand-authored here** — their prompt is *generated by the upstream model session as its final step* (§0.3), filled with the real served PG contract, then run as a normal (bootstrap + that block) app session.

> **🚨 APP TARGET (every `[App]`/`[App/serving]` block) — two live, one dead:** UI → **`frontend/` (Next.js) ONLY**; backend/API → **`app/backend/` (live FastAPI)**; ⛔ **legacy Streamlit UI (`app/streamlit_app.py`, `app/home.py`, `app/pages/`, `app/utils/`) — DO NOT EDIT.** Footgun: `app/` is half-alive (`app/backend/` is live; the rest is dead Streamlit), and Next.js has its own `frontend/app/`. First action in any app session: `cat frontend/package.json` to confirm Next.js; if doing UI work and you open `app/home.py` / `app/pages/*.py`, **STOP — wrong place.** (Full rule: guide §0.2.) A prior session edited the Streamlit UI by mistake (2026-06-18) — this guard prevents a repeat. **Changelog rule: any change the end user would notice ends with a `frontend/data/changelog.json` entry — under the MONDAY of the current week (weeks group Monday→Monday; append to that Monday's block, don't key by the literal ship date).**

**Status legend:** ⬜ open · 🔄 in progress · 🔒 gated · ✅ done (no prompt needed).

```
🎯 **THE NEW MECHANISM (why this is different from every prior null):** E5.4/E13.13/E13.8 all asked "is OUR prediction better than ONE line?" → efficient, PBO≈0.5 (our disagreement = noise). This asks a DIFFERENT question: **"are the BOOKS' OWN markets on a game mutually COHERENT, and where they CONTRADICT each other, which side does the SHARP market imply?"** An edge here does NOT require beating an efficient market on average — it requires the LAZY markets (props, team-totals, alts, F5) to be INCONSISTENT with each other / with the SHARP main line. Books price these on different desks/models at different times → internal inconsistencies are a plausible, untested inefficiency (the sharpest reading of Miller-Davidow). 🔑 the play is RELATIVE (market vs market) → partly market-NEUTRAL: we don't predict the game, we arbitrage the books' own disagreement; our model only picks WHICH side of an inconsistency to take.
SCOPE — the consistency RELATIONS to test (pre-register; cached odds + pitch-settled outcomes):
 1. ⭐ **PROPS → TEAM OFFENSE:** sum the batter prop projections (hits/TB) + implied run-scoring → does it match the **TEAM-TOTAL** line? (props + team-totals = the two LAZIEST markets → most likely inconsistent; highest prior). [needs `team_totals` in S3 — the grab below]
 2. **TEAM-TOTALS → GAME-TOTAL:** home_tt + away_tt ≈ game_total (+ vig wedge); systematic deviation = a play.
 3. **F5 → FULL-GAME = the NEGATIVE CONTROL:** E13.13 found F5 IS correctly derived off the main line (slopes matched) → this relation is EFFICIENT → if our method flags F5-vs-main as inconsistent, the METHOD is broken. Must return "consistent."
```

```
▶ Story prompt — E1.12 REGIME-CONDITIONED SPECIALIZATION — do the models see too-homogeneous a slate? (market-state / mismatch-vs-market segments)   [Model · 🧭 OPUS · ⭐ operator 2026-07-04 hypothesis · CHEAPEST-FIRST bake-off under FULL deflation · a null is a valid deliverable · designed to carry into the fall college markets]   (2026-07-04; post-migration modeling-track ANCHOR — but pullable pre-ASB if a slot frees)
🟢 **READY-TO-RUN (PM 2026-07-19) — TIER-2 edge probe; its designated "post-migration ANCHOR" window is NOW (E11.1 done).** Prompt is current + already lakehouse-aware (S3/DuckDB, SF-free). Sequence it after E13.14 (fresher, market-neutral) — E1.12's mismatch-vs-market leg overlaps what E1.11/E13.8 already found (market usually right when we disagree = a feature-gap lens, not a profit segment), so set the null expectation on MLB main markets and lean into its two edge-independent payoffs (calibration-by-regime for the honest-analytics surface + the sport-agnostic harness that carries into the fall NCAAF/NCAAB thin lines). Diagnose-before-splitting; deflation counts every regime×config.
🎯 THE HYPOTHESIS (operator): our models are market-blind and predict ALL games from ONE homogeneous perspective — maybe that under-fits local structure. Would SPECIALIZING by game "regime" help? Three candidate regimes floated: (a) clear underdog (e.g. +130/-150), (b) no clear favorite / pick'em (-110/-110), (c) teams clearly mismatched by FUNDAMENTALS (W-L, Elo, Pythagorean) but the MARKET favors the lower-graded side. This is regime-conditioning / mixture-of-experts in ML terms — a legitimate way to beat a single global model that only minimizes AVERAGE loss across a heterogeneous distribution.
🧭 PM FRAMING — two DISTINCT ideas are bundled; keep them separate: **(I) market-STATE segmentation** (slice by the line's shape: underdog / pick'em) = conditioning on the market's confidence; **(II) mismatch-vs-market** (fundamentals say A, market says B) = an explicit value/contrarian signal, the only one that names a MECHANISM. Idea II is the interesting one — BUT it is essentially what `best_alpha` already tests: our model IS a fundamentals view, and comparing it to the market IS the edge search. E13.8 + E1.11 both found the market usually RIGHT when we disagree ("market favors the lower-graded team" is usually the market pricing something our features are blind to — gassed bullpen, missing bat, wind — i.e. a FEATURE-GAP detector, not a profit segment). So set expectations: on MLB MAIN markets this most-likely nulls; its real value is (i) calibration, (ii) a feature-gap lens, (iii) the TEMPLATE for the fall less-efficient college markets.
⚠️ **HONEST FRAME — market-blindness / segmentation caveat:** conditioning the model on the LINE to define a regime USES market info for segmentation → this is no longer strictly market-blind. That's fine for a SEGMENTATION study, but state it, and keep `best_alpha=0` honesty intact (no win-rate/edge claims from a lucky regime). Also: defining a regime by the line AND evaluating vs that same line is partially circular (pick'em games are ~50% base-rate BY CONSTRUCTION) → the tight target is CALIBRATION / edge-vs-the-specific-number, not raw accuracy.
🔬 **CHEAPEST-FIRST — do NOT build separate specialists first (the key technical caution):** splitting ~6 seasons into 3 regimes gives each specialist ~1/3 the data + worse variance, and separate specialists almost always LOSE to ONE well-regularized model with regime INTERACTION FEATURES unless the regimes are genuinely distinct data-generating processes. So graduate only on evidence:
 1. **DIAGNOSE first (cheap, no fragmentation):** add regime features + interactions to the EXISTING v6 substrate — a pick'em indicator, line-implied-prob, an Elo/Pythag-vs-market-disagreement flag, and their interactions with the top features. Run a **calibration-by-regime diagnostic**: does predictability / calibration ACTUALLY differ by regime (reliability curves + CRPS/logloss per regime + interaction lift)? This answers the core question without ever splitting the model.
 2. **GRADUATE only if step 1 shows genuine differential signal:** THEN run a proper §0.5 bake-off of ≥3 architectures for capturing it — (a) single model + regime interactions [the foil], (b) a gated mixture-of-experts / regime-router, (c) per-regime specialists — Optuna-tuned, feature-ablated, on the SAME purged/embargoed CV.
🔒 **DEFLATION IS NON-NEGOTIABLE (the E1.11 lesson):** regime-slicing MULTIPLIES the multiple-testing burden. PRE-REGISTER the regime partition + the candidate set BEFORE any eval; count EVERY (regime × config × architecture) toward PBO<0.2 / DSR≥0.95 / FDR; game-level correlated-quote collapse. A specialist that wins in ONE regime out of several TRIED must clear the DEFLATED bar, not its own local one. A clean null (like E1.11) is a valid, informative deliverable — do NOT manufacture a mirage against the ASB clock.
💾 **DATA/COST HYGIENE (§0.5):** read training + regime-defining data (Elo/Pythag/line) from the **S3/DuckDB lakehouse** (a Snowflake pull = RED FLAG); assemble the feature+regime matrix ONCE → parquet; every candidate / ablation / Optuna trial / CV fold reads that cached parquet (never re-read per candidate). State the S3 source + parquet path in the handoff.
🎁 **TWO PAYOFFS THAT DON'T NEED AN EDGE (bank these even on a null):** (i) **calibration-by-regime** — better-calibrated probabilities in a regime are a defensible PRODUCT improvement for the honest-analytics surface (ties E9.26) without beating anyone; (ii) **the framework is the fall multi-sport on-ramp** — "find the least-efficiently-priced segment and specialize" is a LONG shot on liquid MLB main markets but the THESIS for thin NCAAF/NCAAB lines → design the harness sport-agnostic so it re-points at college markets (ties `../../multi_sport_roadmap.md`).
🖥️ **BOX vs LAPTOP:** the diagnostic + bake-off assembly/train is heavy → **assemble-matrix + Optuna are >1-min → operator-run** (state laptop-vs-box + full copy-pasteable commands per the run-command convention); CI (fast pytest + `dbtf compile` if any dbt) on the **LAPTOP**. Lakehouse reads need `-e AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2` if on the box.
GATE/AC: the pre-registration (regime partition + candidate set + gates, BEFORE eval); the calibration-by-regime diagnostic (per-regime reliability + interaction lift) as the graduate/stop decision; IF graduated, the deflated bake-off (≥3 architectures incl. the single-model-with-interactions foil, PBO/DSR/FDR counting every regime×config); honest framing (segmentation-uses-market caveat + `best_alpha` unchanged unless a survivor clears the deflated bar + a promotion runbook before any serve); the calibration deliverable captured for the product surface regardless; the harness left sport-agnostic for the fall. ⇒ either a regime-specialist that survives deflation (→ champion-retrain runbook), or a trustworthy null that the slate is NOT usefully heterogeneous for discrimination (with the calibration + feature-gap findings banked).
```

```
 3. **EDGE TEST (only if it gets there):** the same deflation-honest gate — pre-register, in-fold, PBO/DSR, forward CLV net of the (higher) live vig; wild swings = MANY correlated quotes/game → the E13.13 game/sequence-level collapse is ESSENTIAL or the comparison surface explodes.
```

```
⚠️⚠️ **THE PROP DATA-MINING TRAP (CLAUDE.md — non-negotiable): "find the segment where we'd have won" MANUFACTURES fake edges.** The operator's observation is ANECDOTAL, small-N (personal bets) → could be noise. TEST it properly: pre-register the segments (⭐ the operator's `model_exp − line = −1` UNDER is ONE pre-registered slice — add the symmetric grid Δ ∈ {−2,−1,0,+1,+2} × {over,under}), select IN-FOLD, count EVERY slice toward deflation (PBO<0.2 / DSR≥0.95 / FDR + a PLACEBO control), judge on HELD-OUT / FORWARD CLV — a slice that looks +EV in-sample but fails the deflated gate is REJECTED. ⭐ use the FULL historical prop dataset (all pitchers/games — E5.1 `pitcher_strikeouts` lines vs realized Ks), NOT the operator's personal bets (small-N, selection-biased — that's how the anecdote formed).
```

▶ Story prompt — E10.2 Uncertainty-aware (posterior) bet sizing   [Model/serving · staking-layer correctness · closed-form NOT RL · gated on a PROVEN edge]   (2026-06-24, synthesis)
WHY: standard fractional Kelly assumes the edge is a point estimate. Our Bayesian models produce a POSTERIOR over edge → Kelly on the posterior MEAN systematically OVERBETS because it ignores the variance in the edge estimate itself (the same Jensen's-inequality error that helped kill the totals model). We already SHOW the credible interval on every pick — we should SIZE by it too (on-brand: honest uncertainty → honest stake).
DO (closed-form, NOT RL): stake by integrating expected log-growth over the edge POSTERIOR (or the simpler equivalent: fractional Kelly shrunk by the posterior-CI width) so a wide-CI edge is staked smaller than a tight-CI edge of the same mean. + a cheap CORRELATION DISCOUNT for simultaneous bets sharing systematic risk (same pitching staff / weather / park) so correlated losses don't compound drawdown. Explicitly NOT the RL framing — over-engineering for the core win (revisit RL portfolio optimization only if multi-game effects ever become material; filed, not built).
🔒 GATE/SEQUENCING: this only matters once there's a PROVEN edge to size (E5.2 K props or an E13.13 derivative clearing the CLV gate). Don't build speculatively before an edge exists — but it's the correct sizing layer the moment one does. Cheap. HONEST: it's bet-SIZING correctness (protects the bankroll from the overbet), NOT an edge source.

```
## Epic E6 — Feature-Engineering Audit  🟡 **core delivered via E1.3; gap-analysis DEPRIORITIZED (2026-06-18)**
*E1.3 already delivered the redundancy finding (slim 14/31/19) + the bullpen-dominance ranking; the audit concluded **more features ≠ edge**. Don't run generic new-feature hunting (E6.3); the surviving investment is **bullpen modeling → E2**. Prompts kept below only for a specific bullpen-adjacent hypothesis.*
```
▶ Story prompt — E6.1 ⭐ FEATURE-STORE CORRECTNESS RE-EVALUATION (the WHOLE baseball vertical) → retire the semantically-broken features, then a §0.5 BAKE-OFF + RETRAIN of H2H / TOTALS / RUN_DIFF on the CORRECTED contract   [Model · 🧭 OPUS · 🔬 §0.5 · serving-path · ⭐ CHASING CORRECTNESS, NOT EDGE · runtime-gate discipline]   🟢 READY (beefed-up 2026-08-01, operator — was a thin "feature inventory" stub)
🎯 WHY (the framing is load-bearing — say it out loud): this is a **CORRECTNESS** pass, NOT an edge hunt. `best_alpha=0` is UNCHANGED — we are not adding signal, we are REMOVING inputs that are wrong, mis-scaled, non-stationary, or dead, so the served models are built on features that mean what the model thinks they mean. ⭐ **THE MOTIVATING DEFECT (operator, real):** the TOTALS model's feature importances surface things like **`away_wins` / `away_losses`** as "indicators of total runs" — and those are almost certainly **RAW CUMULATIVE INTEGER COUNTS, not rates/percentages.** A cumulative count GROWS MONOTONICALLY across the season (0 → ~80), so it is **NON-STATIONARY**: it conflates team-quality with HOW-DEEP-INTO-THE-SEASON-WE-ARE, and it means a DIFFERENT thing at serve time (a mid-season partial count) than in training (full-season ranges) — a train/serve covariate-shift bug (the E7.9 class) dressed up as a "feature." A win COUNT should be a win RATE (or a per-game / season-normalized `_seasonnorm` form). ⇒ that a spurious feature "helps" an in-sample metric is NOT a reason to keep it; a wrong feature is a correctness defect even when it's "important."
🔬 **PHASE 1 — AUDIT the SERVED contract (enumerate + classify + FLAG the defects).** For EVERY column in the served champion feature contracts (h2h / totals / run_diff, ALL tiers — the `feature_pregame_game_features` contract + each champion's feature list) classify: family / source / transform / window / platoon; **UNIT** (raw count vs rate vs pct vs z-score vs seasonnorm — is the unit what the name implies? the `away_wins`-is-an-integer check); **STATIONARITY** — ⭐ the key diagnostic: does the feature TREND with `games_played` / date-in-season? (regress each numeric feature on games-played; a strong slope = non-stationary; compare its early-season vs late-season distribution) — a cumulative count is the textbook offender; live pre-game coverage (% non-null at morning serve, the Story-30.3 imputation risk); redundancy / collinearity (near-duplicate or a raw+seasonnorm pair both served); DEAD / unused (in the store but in no champion contract); point-in-time / timing leakage. **Deliverable = a feature-correctness report** classifying every served feature GREEN (correct) / AMBER (fix — e.g. count→rate) / RED (retire), with the defect named per feature.
🔧 **PHASE 2 — FIX or RETIRE the flagged features.** For each AMBER: convert to the correct STATIONARY form (a rate / per-game / `_seasonnorm` variant — many already exist; prefer the existing seasonnorm column over inventing one). For each RED (dead / irreparably-broken / redundant): retire it from the contract. ⚠️ this changes `feature_pregame_game_features_raw` → carry the **INC-19 type-contract** (update the manifest + `gen_type_contract.py --write` in the same change) + train/serve PARITY. Do NOT silently re-scale a served column without re-pinning its contract.
🔬 **PHASE 3 — §0.5 BAKE-OFF + RETRAIN h2h / totals / run_diff on the CORRECTED contract (the "final result").** Re-run the FULL §0.5 discipline per model (≥3 learner classes + a direct-learned foil, Optuna, PURGED/EMBARGOED CV per serving tier, deflation PBO<0.2 / DSR≥0.95 / FDR + placebo, matched foils, TWO-SIDED anchors). ⚠️ **SELECTION-METRIC HYGIENE (E2.1-r):** totals + run_diff are DISCRETE/count targets → gate on RANDOMIZED-PIT flatness + CRPS, keep coverage a FLOOR not a target, score the oracle-floor AND the degenerate-ceiling every run (MAE inverts on a skewed target). Promote via **TD3** (champion-promotion safety) + parity + the **runtime-gate** (serving-path — box-verify the retrained champions serve, features populated, no `intraday_fallback`).
🔒 **HONEST WIN CONDITION (critical — read before judging the retrain):** the target is CORRECTNESS + CALIBRATION, NOT a higher edge/skill number. **Removing a non-stationary artifact (a season-timing proxy) may LOWER an in-sample "skill" metric that was partly the artifact — that is the CORRECT outcome, not a regression.** A model on stationary, correctly-specified features that is calibrated and honest beats a model that scores higher on an in-sample metric it's gaming via a leaked season clock. `best_alpha=0` throughout — no beat-the-market claim.
🔗 SCOPE + COORDINATION: this is the SEMANTICS/correctness lens — DISTINCT from the market-leakage sweep E1.7/E1.8 already did and the E1.9 v6 selection (don't just redo those). **E1.13 (injury-feature + seasonnorm correction → retrain) is a SUBSET of this** (injury features only) — fold/coordinate so we don't retrain twice. ⚠️ LARGE story — Phase 1 (the audit report + corrected-contract proposal) may HAND OFF to a separate Phase-3 retrain session; the audit report GATES the retrain. Data = S3/DuckDB lakehouse (SF-free). Read: the served champion registries + `feature_pregame_game_features` contract + the `_seasonnorm` columns + E2.1-r (selection hygiene) + TD3 + §0.5.
GATE/AC: a feature-correctness report classifying every SERVED h2h/totals/run_diff feature (GREEN/AMBER/RED, defect named + the stationarity diagnostic run); the AMBER features converted to correct stationary forms + the RED features retired (contract + INC-19 type-contract + parity updated); a §0.5 bake-off + retrain of all three models on the corrected contract, deflated + promotion-safe + box-verified; the honest framing recorded (correctness win, `best_alpha=0`, any in-sample metric drop attributed to artifact removal). 🌿 GIT (do this FIRST, before touching any file): `git checkout dev && git pull && git checkout -b <story-branch>`; commit + push to THAT branch, hand back a PR → `dev`. ⛔ NEVER work on / commit to `dev`/`main` directly, ⛔ NEVER `git add -A`; re-check `git branch --show-current` before each commit (a parallel session shares the checkout); any `--publish`/`deploy.sh` is a POST-MERGE operator step. You get to PRE-REGISTER a family; you do not get to DISCOVER one.** Also re-read: the pitcher side's largest H3 lift (`k_pct` +1.713%) belongs to the **PLAYER-STRUCTURE** family (`P4_re_dedup`), NOT to trajectory — carrying "H3's trajectory arms are a real effect" forward without splitting the families mis-attributes a result. Bounds the false-fire rate at every `n`; declares itself **UNDEFINED rather than passed** when `2⁻ⁿ > α`; **weakly STRICTER than the legacy clause at every fold count**, so it can only prevent a false ADD — **verified mechanically to re-decide NONE of the 8 recorded ADDs** (all sit at 8–10 of 11 against a requirement of 8). α=0.20 derived from DESIGN quantities (the tightest end of the legacy clause's own operating range; = `MAX_PBO`), and the α=0.10 sensitivity — which WOULD re-decide 4 of the 8 ADDs — is REPORTED, not hidden. ⚠️ **The `max(...)` is load-bearing and my own guard caught its absence:** a fixed-α sign test asymptotically demands a rate → 0.50, so past **n ≈ 31** the calibrated count alone would be LOOSER than 60%. 🪤 **THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN THE SHARED INSTRUMENTS.** (1) `null_analysis`'s DSR extrapolation — the THIRD in that function after E7.15-H3's two — `np.resize` TILES the skill series, inflating its `ddof=1` Sharpe by ≈`√(n/(n−1))` and **non-monotonically**, while a single-element `trial_sharpes` made `V` fall back to `1/n_obs` computed on the RESIZED length, so the benchmark melted away as folds were added. **Every recorded `folds_needed_DSR` was wrong** (H3 `bb_pct` 140 → **372**; three are **UNREACHABLE at any n** — two of which E7.15's prose correction had independently reached). There is not even a space at the boundary (`T WallsW Aloy(M)` = "T Walls" + "W Aloy(M)"). Splitting requires a name-pattern tokenizer: a player = `<initial(s)> <surname>` + optional `(status)`, where the boundary is the next capital-letter initial. **It MUST handle the hard cases the fixture deliberately contains: dotted multi-initials (`J.P. Crawford`, `C.J. Kayfus`, `A.J. Blubaugh`), hyphenated surnames (`I Kiner-Falefa`, `C Encarnacion-Strand`), and `Jr.`/suffix names (`V Mesa Jr.`, `L Wade Jr.`).** Do NOT ship a naive split — pin the parser with a fixture test that reproduces the full grid's player count per team.

Surface unmatched rows for review.
 • **AVAILABILITY DERIVATION:** a board prospect is AVAILABLE iff their MLBAM id matches NO player in ANY team × ANY slot (including `(M)`/`(I)`/`(R)`); everyone in the grid is rostered. Show WHO rosters a taken player (the row/team) + their slot-status.

▶ Story prompt — E8.3 BOARD-COVERAGE REPORT: get the flagged-missing prospects OUT of the app and into the board build   [App + data · 🧭 SONNET · gated on E8.2b shipped · from the operator 2026-08-02]
🎯 WHY: E8.2b captures prospects a league rosters that our board does NOT carry — the money signal, because *someone spent a dynasty roster spot on him*. On the first real league it named exactly the three the operator had found by hand (`C.J. Kayfus`, `V Honeycutt`, `D Lesko`). **But the capture currently has NO EGRESS: copy-as-CSV to the clipboard is the only way out.** Nothing writes to S3, no ticket, nothing the board build reads. So today it is a reliable CHECKLIST and not a HANDOFF — whoever regenerates the board still has to be told by a human, which is exactly the step that gets skipped.
📦 **WHAT EXISTS TODAY (read before designing — three different things, only two of them persisted):** (a) the admin's `missing_from_board` flag IS persisted, in DynamoDB on the USER item under the `mlb_leagues` map, so it survives reload/re-upload as long as the entry key matches; (b) the uploaded roster is persisted, so the AUTO-SUGGESTED gaps (an unresolved player sitting in a minors slot) regenerate on every read; (c) the REPORT itself is derived — `board_match.RosterMatch.coverage_gaps`, recomputed per read, never stored. (c) is deliberate and should stay: a derived report self-corrects when the board is republished.
🔨 DO: (1) a way for an admin to GET the flagged players out — the deliverable is a report they can act on, not another screen to remember to visit. (2) ⚠️ **the flags are siloed PER USER** (`dynamo.list_mlb_leagues(user_id)`), so an admin sees only their OWN today; if the report is meant to cover all users' uploads it needs a cross-user read, which is a NEW privacy decision — state it explicitly rather than quietly widening the scope of data an admin can see. (3) close the loop into the board build if a durable path is cheap (e.g. a known S3 key the E8.0 board runner reads on its next run) — but a plain scheduled/on-demand report is an acceptable, honest floor.
⛔ **EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — AUTO-ADDING A FLAGGED PLAYER TO THE BOARD (operator decision 2026-08-02, do NOT re-litigate):** a new prospect cannot just be appended; he has to be run through the projection, and that **re-ranks the board**. A board that silently reorders because someone uploaded a roster is bad UX and worse provenance (the 8/3-draft lesson: you must know WHICH file you drafted from). Board membership stays a deliberate, versioned build step. This story routes the SIGNAL to that build; it never bypasses it.
🐛 **FOLD IN THIS KNOWN DEFECT (found 2026-08-02, small):** a confirmed `missing_from_board` override is applied in `board_match.match_roster` PASS 1, **before any matching is attempted** — so once the board actually ADDS that player, he stays flagged as a gap and stays OUT of the rostered overlay until the admin clears the flag by hand. The auto-SUGGESTED gaps have no such problem (recomputed from scratch, they drop off the moment a player resolves). Fix = attempt the match first and honour the flag only if it still fails; then the flag becomes self-healing and this story's report shrinks on its own as the board catches up. ⭐ that self-healing is what makes the report trustworthy — a list that only ever grows stops being read.
🚨 APP-TARGET GUARD: UI = `frontend/` (Next.js) ONLY; backend = `app/backend/`; ⛔ never legacy Streamlit. **ADMIN-GATED, same gate as E8.1/E8.2 — the MLB board is not public until 2027; do NOT wire a public entitlement.**
🖥️ CONSTRAINTS: SF-free (DuckDB/S3); privacy-minimal — this is the USER's league data, so any widening of who can read it is a stated decision, not a side effect; `best_alpha=0` unchanged. Own session branch off `dev`, PR to `dev`. ⚠️ the API Lambda ships ONLY via `./infrastructure/lambda/deploy.sh` (post-merge operator step) — `frontend/` auto-deploys, the backend does not (NF-C0).
GATE/AC: an admin can obtain the flagged-missing list outside the browser session (not clipboard-only); the per-user-silo question answered explicitly one way or the other; the stale-confirmed-flag defect fixed with a test that proves a flagged player REJOINS the overlay once the board carries him; auto-add-to-board confirmed out of scope; CI green (fast + slow gates); changelog line ONLY if the surface is user-visible (it is admin-only today, so likely none). Operator handoff incl. the post-merge `deploy.sh` step.

```
▶ Story prompt — E7.11 Multi-source prospect-ranking CONSENSUS (beyond FanGraphs)   [Data · 🧭 SONNET · feeds E8.0/E8.1 board + E7.12 tool-grade priors · from the operator stretch ask 2026-07-29]
✅ **CODE-COMPLETE 2026-07-29 — report: `ablation_results/e7_11_prospect_consensus.md`.** MLB Pipeline (Top 100 + all 30 org Top 30s) ingested → `baseball/milb/mlb_pipeline_rankings` (S3 Delta); consensus + residual disagreement + our-MLE-vs-consensus shipped as `betting_ml/scripts/prospect_board/{mlb_pipeline,consensus,build_consensus,build_consensus_assembly}.py`. Verified end-to-end on the real lake: **1,451-player universe** (1,286 board ∪ **165 Pipeline-only**), 9-tab workbook + CSVs.
 • ⭐ **Pipeline publishes the MLBAM id directly** (`Person:<id>` = the E7.4 spine) ⇒ **100.0% of 1,000 rows / 900 players keyed with ZERO name matching** — the leg E7.4 refused to build. Bonus: 20-80 tool grades parsed from the scouting PROSE (their grade FIELDS are all NULL) on 994/1,000 → a second independent grade set for E7.12.
 • 🚦 **ACCESS PROBED, NOT ASSUMED:** `/prospects/` is robots-PERMITTED (page read) but **`data-graph.mlb.com` — the JSON API the page's own JS calls — is `Disallow: /` and is NEVER CALLED.** That is *why* the ingest parses HTML; a source-inspection test fails CI if a future session "simplifies" it into a data-graph request, and the ingest re-reads robots every run and RAISES if `/prospects/` is ever disallowed. **Prospects Live was probed and REFUSED on its own robots** (`ClaudeBot Disallow: /` + `ai-train=no`; ranking routes 404 anonymously) ⇒ it joins BA/Law/ESPN/BP on the MANUAL hand-key path (`--manual name=file.csv`; deterministic id / name+org legs only; unresolved rows REPORTED, never guessed).
 • ⭐ **THE FINDING — two respected sources agree far less than they look like they do:** Spearman ρ **0.592** overall (n=62 both-ranked), **0.655** within-org (n=735, median |diff| **6 places of 30**), plus 165 players one ranks and the other doesn't carry. That is the case for a consensus as a NUMBER — not a claim that averaging is more accurate (untested; `best_alpha=0`).
 • 🧨 **FOUR load-bearing decisions, each pinned by a test:** (a) partial coverage is AVERAGED OVER, never imputed (a Top-100 source has said nothing about #340; it did not rank him 101st); (b) a 1-source "consensus" is labelled as one and its `rank_spread` is **NULL, not 0.0** — `max−min` over one value renders as "every source agrees exactly", the opposite of what one opinion means; (c) every disagreement is a **RESIDUAL** (raw-gap tail bias ≈20.6 pctile pts → residual ≈3.6, **−82%**, vs a 15-pt flag threshold) via the now-SHARED `board_assembly.residual_vs_fit`, so the E8.0 regression-to-mean lesson is learned once — its LINEAR fit leaves a little tail curvature, stated not hidden; (d) 🚨 **a source cannot disagree with a consensus it ALONE constitutes** — the first real run showed a lopsided 89-vs-35 flag split caused purely by comparing 1-source rows against themselves through two different percentile denominators; restricting to `n_sources≥2` made it 64/63 and 100/130.
 • ⚠️ Overall and org rank SCOPES are aggregated separately (org rank 1 on a thin farm ≠ overall rank 1); `mle_vs_consensus` is fitted within player-type × scope for the same reason (`consensus_scope_used` says which frame each row was judged in). Our line vs consensus: 1,276 comparable, 194 we're-higher / 207 consensus-higher.
 • 🕰️ **HISTORY INGESTED (operator ask): 2010–2026, ~17 seasons** = the substrate for ASSESSING these rankings. Ranks are genuinely point-in-time (2015 = Buxton/Bryant/Correa; 2019 = Guerrero/Tatís; 2023 = Henderson/Carroll). Depth probed: ≤2008 EMPTY · **2010–2011 = Top 50 not Top 100** (absence there is a WEAKER statement) · 2012+ = Top 100. 🚨 **TWO LEAKAGE TRAPS, both closed, both invisible because the RANK beside them is correctly historical:** (i) the page's `Person`/`Team` entities are **LIVE** — 2015-page Buxton returns age **32** (was 21), Bryant returns **COL** (was a Cub) ⇒ every such field suffixed **`_current`**; unsuffixed `org` comes ONLY from an org-list URL (genuinely as-of); `birth_date` stays unsuffixed because age-as-of-season is derivable from it leakage-free. (ii) the bio list runs **PAST** the season — the 2015 page carries 2016/2017/2018 reports for 65/100 players and my first cut took the NEWEST ⇒ `_select_bio` now takes the season's own report or the newest NOT AFTER it + stamps `bio_season` (verified 100/100 era-matched, ZERO future bios). (iii) a past season stamps `as_of=<season>-02-01`, never today (stamping a 2015 board 2026-07-29 places it AFTER every outcome it predicts).
 • ⚠️ **THE ACCURACY STUDY ITSELF IS NOT RUN HERE** — it is E7.8-shaped (realized outcome with never-arrived = ZERO to dissolve survivorship · leave-one-cohort-out CV with a PLAYER purge · PBO/DSR/FDR). Harness already exists: `betting_ml/scripts/fv_translation/` — pointing it at `mlb_pipeline_rankings` is a bounded follow-on and genuinely new (E7.8 measured FV; nobody has measured Pipeline; a head-to-head on ONE cohort under ONE gate beats either alone). Inherits E7.8's small-N ceiling: rules out a LARGE effect, not a small one. `best_alpha=0` stands.
 • ⛔ **BA / KEITH LAW VERDICT (operator ask, probed 2026-07-29) — REFUSE, for two DIFFERENT reasons.** **Baseball America** serves a **Cloudflare managed challenge on `/robots.txt` ITSELF** — we cannot even read its policy. This repo DOES run a solver (Byparr) for FanGraphs, which is exactly why the line matters: FanGraphs' board is free-to-view + CSV-exportable, whereas BA's rankings ARE the paid product ⇒ solving the challenge here would be defeating an access control to take PAYWALLED content. **The Athletic** (Law) carries a prose **NYT rights reservation explicitly banning automated scraping, text/data mining, AI/ML/LLM development, cached datasets, AND commercial use** — four independent grounds. Both stay hand-key-only (`--manual`; verified 100% resolution on a 40-row file via the name+org leg). **Cost of the refusal, stated:** the overall consensus stays 2 sources deep (62 players ≥2 ranks); a hand-keyed Top 100 would roughly double it — a ~20-min annual typing job for a subscriber. ⭐ BA's real research value is its **~30-park MiLB PARK FACTORS** (E7.12 #1), not its rankings — hand-keyable annually, or computable ourselves from free game logs.
 • ✅ **BACKFILL RAN + SPOT-CHECKED 2026-07-29: 17 seasons, 14,455 rows, 100% MLBAM id on every season, as_of correct on every one, and ZERO rows graded off a post-season report** (the anti-leakage receipt). 4 anomalies chased: 2011-`dbacks` + 2014-`bluejays` are UPSTREAM-EMPTY (MLB declares limit:30, serves `[]`) → correctly recorded as not-published, not a failure; 2020/2021 Top 100 is genuinely **99** deep upstream (ranks 1–99, no gaps/dupes); 🚨 **ORG-LIST DEPTH CHANGES BY ERA — Top 10 (2011) / Top 20 (2012-2014) / Top 30 (2015+)** ⇒ an org rank of 15 is mid-pack in 2023 and DIDN'T EXIST in 2013, and "absent from the 2013 org list" = outside the top **20**. This matters MORE than the Top-50 overall fact because the org scope carries the breadth (735 vs 62 two-source players) — now `ORG_LIST_DEPTH_BY_ERA`, warned on pre-2015, and the OBSERVED depth is surfaced per run (authoritative; the constants are a summary). 🐛 **ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND + FIXED: `.isdigit()` is not "is a year"** — a live `contentTitle` of `"201"` parsed as the year 201, which sorts BELOW every real season and so quietly wins the "newest bio not after the season" fallback, reporting `bio_season=201` (1 row of 14,455; no leakage possible since it's in the past). ▶ Story prompt — E7.12-S2 SURVIVORSHIP / promotion selection-bias correction on the MiLB→MLB MLE   [Model · 🧭 OPUS · 🔬 §0.5 · E7.12 slice 2 · extends E7.3/E7.3p]   ✅ RUN 2026-07-31 — report `ablation_results/e7_12_slice2_survivorship{,_pitchers}.md`
```
```
🧾 **BUILT/RUN NOTES — five things the spec did not anticipate, all of which changed the design.** (1) **ATTRITION IS THE DOMINANT COMPETING RISK, not a refinement.** The spec's hazard treats a never-promoted player as censored; in fact **85% of them LEAVE affiliated ball** and the mean at-risk window is **2.05 seasons**, so `P(promote in 4) = 1-∏(1-h)` over-predicts by **~2.2×** (mature-cohort observed/expected 0.46). A second `exited` hazard + a two-state walk brings it to **0.94 / 0.98**. A never-promoted player's last season means CENSORED (still playing at the calendar edge) or EXITED (left) and those must never be collapsed. (2) **THE CENSORING GUARD WAS VERIFIED ON SYNTHETIC AND STILL FAILED ON REAL DATA** — see the roadmap note; verifying a guard on synthetic verifies its MECHANISM, not its THRESHOLD. (3) **STABILIZED IPW IS NOT A DISTINCT ARM HERE** — weights are normalised to mean 1, so a constant numerator cancels exactly and the arm is byte-identical to raw IPW (and a calendar-only numerator model cancels too, since a FIXED horizon evaluates every player at the same season indices). Replaced with **inverse-ODDS** `(1-p)/p`, which targets the UN-PROMOTED population and is arguably the truer estimand for a board that scores players who have not debuted. (4) 🚨 **A HECKMAN CORRECTION IS ONLY A CORRECTION IF λ IS ZEROED AT PREDICT TIME** — fitted with λ and predicted with each player's own λ, the model reproduces `E[Y|X,S=1]`, the biased quantity (synthetic: 1.443, WORSE than doing nothing at 1.424; zeroing λ → 0.803, removing 43.6% of the planted bias). **The live gate scores GRADUATES, for whom carrying λ is correct — so the live gate CANNOT validate the Heckman arm as a bias fix, and a Heckman arm that clears it would correct nothing for prospects unless emission zeroes λ.** (5) the S2 baseline must be the **SHIPPED slice-1 config per metric**, and an IPW weight must **MULTIPLY** the shipped label-precision weight — otherwise the run re-books the slice-1 win, or confounds "add IPW" with "remove label weighting".
🎯 WHY: **the MLE is fit on GRADUATES ONLY and SERVED on PROSPECTS** — two populations that overlap at a 7.5% promotion rate (736 of 9,804 batters ever debut). 🛑 **CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS PROMPT — get the statistics right or the whole slice is mis-aimed.** An earlier version said promotion being decided on the minor line is "selection ON THE PREDICTOR, which biases the translation slope." **That is BACKWARDS.** Selection on an OBSERVED covariate leaves `E[Y|X]` unbiased — it is the textbook HARMLESS case, and a model conditioning on X is fine under it. The two things that DO motivate this slice are: **(a) SELECTION ON UNOBSERVABLES** — scouts promote on tools, makeup, health and org need, none of which we measure, and all of which plausibly predict MLB performance; if `corr(selection error, outcome error) ≠ 0` the translation IS biased (the Heckman case); and **(b) THE ESTIMAND** — we fit where the data is dense (good prospects who got promoted) and serve where it is sparse (the prospect population at large). Even with unbiased coefficients, the fit is optimised for the wrong population. **(b) is the more defensible motivation and should lead.** Note what this implies: **IPW does NOT fix selection on unobservables** (it fixes selection on observables, under which the conditional mean was already fine) — IPW's job here is the ESTIMAND, re-weighting training toward the population we actually serve. Measured on the existing artifacts: only **10.6% of batter (player, level) rows carry an MLB label (2,171 of 20,561)** and **12.7% of pitcher rows (3,027 of 23,862)** — 18,390 / 20,835 never debut. And the selection is **LEVEL-DEPENDENT**, so it cannot be absorbed by a global intercept: labelled-rate runs Single-A 0.07 → Double-A 0.12 → Triple-A 0.14 (batters) and 0.075 → 0.166 → 0.185 (pitchers). This is the largest un-modelled effect left in the MLE.
🚨 **RIGHT-CENSORING — MEASURED 2026-07-31, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING TO SOLVE: 37.3% of the "never-MLB" population (3,385 of 9,068 batters) was STILL ACTIVE in MiLB in 2023+, and 1,921 were playing in 2026.** "Has not debuted" ≠ "will not debut" — those players are IN PROGRESS, not failures. A naive `debuted 0/1` propensity model would learn **"recent players do not get promoted,"** which is FOLLOW-UP TIME, not selection — and IPW would then inflate the weights on exactly the most recent cohorts, which is the opposite of the intended correction. ⇒ **use a DISCRETE-TIME HAZARD formulation** (`P(promote in season s | not promoted before s)`, censoring a player at their last observed MiLB season), which handles this natively; a follow-up restriction (only players with ≥N years of post-MiLB follow-up) is the cruder fallback and throws away 37% of the population. **Pre-register which, and report the promotion base rate by last-MiLB-season either way — a propensity model whose fitted promotion rate declines monotonically in recency has learned the censoring.**
🧭 STEP 0 — LOCATE (do first): (a) ⚠️ **THE PAIRS ARTIFACT CARRIES NO SEASON FOR UN-PROMOTED PLAYERS** — `debut_cohort` is populated for GRADUATES ONLY, so a leakage-safe in-fold propensity fit is not expressible against the current parquet. `build_graduated_pairs{,_pitchers}.py` must be extended to carry a per-(player, level) **`first_minor_season` / `last_minor_season`** (both are a trivial `min`/`max` over the same `player_game_logs` scan it already runs). Do this FIRST; everything else depends on it. (b) the un-promoted population itself is **ALREADY IN THE ARTIFACT** — `mle_graduated_pairs{,_pitchers}.parquet` carry `is_prospect` / `has_mlb_label` for every (player, level) row, so **NO new ingest is needed**; (b) the fit is `milb_mle.PartialPoolProjector`, which **already accepts `weight_col`** (added by E7.12 slice 1) — that is exactly the wiring an IPW arm needs, so do not re-plumb it; (c) the harness, folds, deflation, anchors and the enforced BH-FDR gate are all in `run_e7_12_slice1.py` — REUSE it (`SideConfig` + a ladder), do not fork.
🔬 DO — pre-register ≥3 candidate corrections, LEARNER HELD FIXED at each metric's pinned incumbent prior scale (the E7.9 lesson; slice 1's precedent): (a) **IPW** — a promotion-propensity model `P(debut | minor line, age, level, league)` fit on the FULL population, graduates weighted `1/p̂`; (b) **HECKMAN two-stage** — a selection equation plus the inverse Mills ratio as an outcome-equation regressor; (c) a **JOINT promotion/performance** model. Report the propensity model's OWN calibration + AUC separately (see the epistemic limit below — it is the only direct evidence the selection mechanism was captured at all).
⭐ **THE DIRECTIONAL FALSIFICATION FOR THIS SLICE — STRATIFY THE HELD-OUT SCORE BY PROPENSITY.** We can never score on the un-promoted, but the **LOW-PROPENSITY GRADUATES are their closest observable proxy** — players who look like the un-promoted population and happened to get through. ⇒ **pre-register that a real survivorship correction's benefit must CONCENTRATE in the bottom propensity tercile** and be ~0 in the top tercile. A correction that improves high-propensity graduates just as much is **generic re-weighting, not selection correction** — the exact analogue of slice 1's "the park lift must concentrate in the ball-in-play metrics," which is the test that caught the pitcher park claim. Report the per-tercile lift whether or not it holds.
⚙️ **WHAT THE HARNESS CAN AND CANNOT EXPRESS TODAY (checked 2026-07-31):** **IPW needs NO new plumbing** — `PartialPoolProjector` already accepts `weight_col` (E7.12 slice 1), so an IPW arm is just an `ipw_weight` column on the pairs. **HECKMAN DOES need a small additive change**: the Mills ratio is an extra REGRESSOR, and `MleConfig.aux_cols` is read by `GBMProjector` ONLY — the pool's design is hardcoded to `(intercept, minor, age)` + the level/league blocks. Add an optional `extra_cols` that joins the UNPENALIZED fixed block, defaulting to none = byte-exact incumbent, pinned by a test (the same discipline `weight_col` shipped under). ⚠️ Heckman without an **EXCLUSION RESTRICTION** (something that moves promotion but not MLB performance — org need at the position is the plausible candidate; draft position is NOT, it proxies talent) is identified only off the Mills ratio's nonlinearity, which is notoriously fragile — state which you have.
🪤 ANCHORS — the slice-1 carry-over, non-negotiable (a re-weighting slice lies in exactly the way the park slice did: **dividing by / weighting with any dispersed number shifts MAE whether or not the mechanism is real**): **`A_propensity_placebo`** = the SAME propensities PERMUTED WITHIN LEVEL — must LOSE (catches "any dispersed weight helps"; the direct analogue of `A_park_placebo`, which was the arm that killed the pitcher park claim); **`A_uniform_weight`** = the incumbent by construction; and **REPORT EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE PER FOLD** — IPW weights explode at low propensity, so clip and show the ESS, because an arm that has traded bias for variance must be visible as having done so. ⚠️ The eval population must be IDENTICAL across arms (`run_ladder` already ASSERTS this) — IPW changes TRAINING weights, never the scored rows.
⚠️ **THE EPISTEMIC LIMIT — STATE IT UP FRONT, IT IS NOT A CAVEAT TO ADD AT THE END.** We can only ever score on players who WERE promoted. So the gate measures *"does modelling selection improve prediction ON GRADUATES"* — which is **strictly weaker** than *"removes the bias"*. A correction can be theoretically right and still not improve held-out graduate MAE. ⇒ **pre-register that a NULL here is genuinely AMBIGUOUS**, unlike slice 1 where a null was a clean null: it means either "no selection bias" or "the correction cannot be validated on the observable population." Do not report an ambiguous null as a clean one. Consider a synthetic-truth check (simulate a known selection process, verify each correction RECOVERS the planted coefficient) as the only way to distinguish those two readings — that is this slice's oracle floor.
⚖️ GATE/AC: held-out translation lift over the incumbent on the purged leave-one-debut-cohort-out folds, in ≥60% of cohorts, surviving **BH-FDR over the metric family (now ENFORCED, not reported)**; the placebo must lose; ESS reported per fold; the synthetic-truth recovery check reported. A null add is DROPPED. Run BOTH sides (batters and pitchers) — the labelled-rate gradient is steeper on pitchers (0.075→0.185), so if the effect is real it should be LARGER there, and that is a free directional falsification. `best_alpha = 0`. 🌿 GIT (do this FIRST, before touching any file): `git checkout dev && git pull && git checkout -b <story-branch>`; commit + push to THAT branch, hand back a PR → `dev`. ⛔ NEVER work on / commit to `dev`/`main` directly, ⛔ NEVER `git add -A`; re-check `git branch --show-current` before each commit (a parallel session shares the checkout); any `--publish`/`deploy.sh` is a POST-MERGE operator step. Blocks are **penalized** so they estimate departures from the linear main effect that already ships (this is why the slice is not "add age"). **S2 confound handled as BOTH prompt options at once:** `V_ipw_Y0`/`V_ipw_Y2` re-run baseline+interaction under S2's `T1b_ipw_odds` inverse-odds weights, and `survivorship_read` takes the SECOND difference (re-weighted lift ÷ unweighted lift) so the re-weighting sits on both sides and can't be mistaken for the mechanism; retention floor **0.50** pre-registered, below which the verdict is **`UPPER_BOUND_ONLY`**. **Direct-learned ceiling probe** `R_gbm_age`/`R_gbm_noage` (§0.5) — a matched GBM pair differing only in whether age is visible, bounding how much age structure is exploitable at ALL independent of our bucketing; non-selectable, because E7.9 measured 54-77% of every apparent margin in this program as the learner swap. **`synthetic_recovery_check` proves the machinery discriminates BEFORE any null is trusted** (NF1.7 lesson 1): planted slope → slope arm +18.1% / intercept arm −0.07%; planted intercept → intercept +14.2% / slope +0.00%; null panel → neither above 0.11%. ⚠️ **THIS SLICE IS CONFOUNDED WITH S2 AND MUST NOT BE RUN BLIND TO IT.** A young player who did NOT develop never gets promoted, so **any age effect estimated on graduates alone is entangled with selection** — "young players' lines translate better" is precisely the claim survivorship bias manufactures out of nothing. ⇒ run AFTER S2 and either (i) carry S2's best correction as a covariate/weight, or (ii) pre-register explicitly that the age effect is being measured on the selected population and is therefore an upper bound. State which; do not leave it implicit. `best_alpha = 0`.
```

```
📌 **WHAT A RE-OPENER NEEDS TO KNOW (the three things that cost this session time, and the one scheduled trigger):**
1. 🚨 **THE RETAINED BOARD'S `level` IS A ONE-SIDED OUTCOME LEAK.** FanGraphs serves the retained past board with `level` updated to the player's CURRENT level: on the 2018–2022 cohort, `level='MLB'` holds 2,035 debuts + 1,258 non-debuts while `level ∈ {A,A+,AA,AAA}` holds 1,908 rows of which **exactly ONE debuted** — i.e. a minor-league level on a retained board is near-certain proof the player busted. (2) ⛔ **a scheduled cancellation is represented by TWO independent Stripe fields — the legacy `cancel_at_period_end` boolean AND a separate `cancel_at` timestamp; on FLEXIBLE billing mode the Customer Portal populates `cancel_at`, not the boolean** → checking only one field silently reports "not canceled." Treat EITHER as "scheduled to cancel"; check the SDK's own type stubs for every field that can represent the same real-world state. ⇒ RUNTIME-GATE: billing status must be verified against the live Stripe dashboard post-deploy — CI/unit tests cover the "obvious shape", not the SDK's real object semantics.
```

```
STRUCTURE (the approved layout — keep it tight, ~70% less copy than v1):
  1. Small eyebrow ("Credence Sports").
```

```
▶ Story prompt — E10.1 Parlay decision-support calculator (honest MVP)   [Model + App]
✅ **READY-STAMP (2026-07-08) — a strong on-brand parallel to E11.20/E9.43/E9.26.** 🔒 **THIS IS THE CALCULATOR, NOT THE RECOMMENDER:** show the user the TRUTH about a parlay they build (true combined prob vs book-implied + EV + an honest "most parlays are −EV after vig" verdict) — do NOT surface/"recommend" +EV parlays (that's E10.3, HARD-gated behind a proven edge we do NOT have; `best_alpha=0` holds). Honest-framing banned-language scan applies (no +EV/value/edge language; the −EV verdict is the point). ⭐ **PARALLEL-SAFETY (surface-disjoint from the 3 active sessions) — hold ALL of these:** (1) build it on its OWN parlay page/route — NOT pick-detail (E9.43's surface) and NOT the performance page (E9.26's); (2) read per-leg model probs via the **SERVING CACHE (DynamoDB→S3), NOT a direct `daily_model_predictions`/mart/lakehouse query** (the E9.40 discipline — those marts may be mid-Delta-migration under E11.20); dedup-to-latest per game (the E11.22 concern, already satisfied by `write_serving_store` on the cached blob); (3) same-game correlation = use an EXISTING/derived source (Epic 22.1 pairwise), source-stamped — do NOT build a NEW correlation pipeline over the lakehouse/box mid-E11.20; (4) OFF-BOX — frontend (Vercel) + a stateless backend calc endpoint (`app/backend/`), no serving-store-write/dbt/box. 🚨 APP-TARGET GUARD: UI=`frontend/` only; backend=`app/backend/` only; ⛔ never legacy Streamlit; `cat frontend/package.json` first. Changelog (user-facing). E10.5 (the fuller frontend parlay surface) can follow.
Read: §5G E10.1 + §0 + master Epic 22.1 (pairwise correlation) + the E9.40 scorecard (`services/scorecard.py`) for the serving-cache read + win-semantics pattern to reuse + `test_k_projection_serving.py` (the honest banned-language scan to extend).
🎯 WHAT: a build-your-own-parlay CALCULATOR that tells the user the TRUTH about the parlay they assemble — true combined probability (model) vs the book's implied probability (parlay price) + EV + a plain-language verdict — with same-game legs correlation-adjusted, not naively multiplied. Education/transparency, not a bet rec.
DO:
 0. **LEG UNIVERSE (Task 0 — sizes it):** which served markets can be legs? Start with the markets that already carry a MODEL probability in the serving cache — moneyline (`model_prob` / h2h), total_runs (over/under), and K-props (E5.5 pitcher strikeouts) if a per-leg prob is available. Cross-market legs allowed. Confirm each leg type exposes a model prob + a book price via the serving cache.
 1. **PER-LEG:** for each leg pull the **model probability** (via the SERVING CACHE — the E9.40 discipline, dedup-to-latest per game; NOT a direct mart/lakehouse query) + the **book price** (the odds the user is taking). Convert book odds → book-implied prob (de-vig per-leg where sensible, but the parlay-level implied comes from the parlay PRICE — see #3).
 2. **TRUE COMBINED PROBABILITY:** for legs in DIFFERENT games (independent) = product of per-leg model probs. For **SAME-GAME legs = correlation-ADJUSTED, never the naive product** (naive independence OVERSTATES same-game parlay prob = dishonest in the user's favor — the exact thing this tool exists to prevent). Use an EXISTING/derived pairwise-correlation source (Epic 22.1), **source-stamped**; if no correlation is available for a same-game pair, FLAG it + use a documented conservative adjustment — do NOT silently assume independence.
 3. **BOOK-IMPLIED + EV:** cross-game parlay price = product of per-leg decimal odds (computable). Same-game/SGP → the book prices it with its OWN correlation model, so the honest MVP takes the **user-entered book parlay odds** as the price (we can't infer the SGP price — that's E10.2's feasibility spike; note it). implied = 1/decimal_parlay_odds; **EV per $1 = true_prob × decimal_parlay_odds − 1**.
 4. **VERDICT (plain language, honest):** e.g. "The book's price implies {implied}%; the model estimates {true}%. Expected value ≈ {EV}% per $1 — this parlay is −EV" (or the rare ≥0 case shown factually, NOT as a "+EV play" — no recommend language). Always state that most parlays are −EV after vig.
 5. **UI (own parlay page/route — NOT pick-detail/performance):** add/remove legs (pick game → market → side; pull or enter the odds), live combined true-vs-implied + EV + verdict as legs change; a same-game-correlation-applied badge; edge-case handling (a leg with no served model prob → flag/exclude, don't fabricate).
🚨 APP-TARGET GUARD: UI=`frontend/` only (`cat frontend/package.json` first); backend=`app/backend/` (a STATELESS calc endpoint reading the serving cache — no serving-store-write/dbt/box); ⛔ never legacy Streamlit. 🔒 honest-framing banned-language scan EXTENDED to the new parlay components + green; `best_alpha=0`/`is_bet_recommendation=False` intact; NO "+EV parlay"/value/edge framing (E10.3 territory, hard-gated). Changelog (user-facing).
GATE/AC: for any user-built parlay — returns true combined prob (same-game correlation-adjusted + source-stamped, conservative-flagged when no source) vs book-implied + EV + an honest plain-language verdict; cross-game computed, same-game uses the user-entered book price (SGP-pricing gap noted → E10.2); serving-cache-only reads (insulated from E11.20); honest framing verified by the extended scan; a leg without a model prob is handled gracefully; changelog; CI green (unit tests on the prob/EV/correlation math + the honest scan). Closeout: ⏭️ operator handoff + `git add` + changelog. E10.5 (fuller parlay surface) + E10.2 (SGP-price feasibility) can follow.
```

healthy the whole time, so every existing check was blind. This is the INC-37 / E9.48 / Byparr class: a
frozen DERIVED artifact is invisible to a freshness check on its SOURCE. The lineup monitor read a 6.5h-stale
parquet and reported "no newly confirmed lineups" ~40 times while the op returned SUCCESS every 30 min.

DO:

     timestamp IN THE DATA (max(ingestion_ts) / a build/as-of column — NOT the S3 LastModified) against now,
     and page via send_alert when the lag exceeds a DECLARED per-artifact cadence.
     ⚠️ ⛔ NEVER use `aws s3 ls` LastModified (E11.20 phase-2a: it prints SHELL-LOCAL time, and #638 just made
        the S3 writes ATOMIC via server-side copy → a re-copied file keeps a fresh mtime even when the DATA is
        stale). Read the parquet CONTENT.

  2. REGISTER stg_statsapi_lineups_wide FIRST (the INC-41 victim) with its real cadence (it rebuilds each

     W12/W9 "the check cadence must match the write cadence" lesson). Then add the other serving-critical
     intraday parquet (the feature-store blocks predict_today reads).

     (E11.30 — an ALERT-tier op that only logs is the exact failure this card exists to fix). An

     os.environ keys — instance-role (make_s3_client() / DuckDB credential_chain).

     producer manufactures a false stale-alarm on the newest slate) AND a scheduled OFF-CYCLE check, so an
     intraday freeze (INC-41's exact shape) is caught BETWEEN daily runs, not only at the next daily.

```
▶ Story prompt — E9.56 🔒 API ENTITLEMENT HARDENING + ANTI-SCRAPE — the paid/gated data must NOT be retrievable from the network payload (server-side enforcement, NOT endpoint obfuscation)   [App/backend · 🧭 OPUS (serving-path + security-critical) · ⛔ PRE-LAUNCH BLOCKER for the public fantasy launch (NF3.2 + E9.45) · from operator 2026-08-01]   🟢 READY — ⏭️ SEQUENCED LAST (operator 2026-08-01: pushing feature breadth first, then harden the paywall right before launch) → the split is DECIDED, ENFORCED late; ⚠️ do NOT flip the app truly public until this lands (2026 data is liftable off the wire until then)
🎯 WHY (operator): the app's endpoints + JSON payloads are visible in browser dev-tools (Network tab), so a sophisticated user can read them directly / replay the request — and once we go PUBLIC with a freemium split (NF3.2: past-seasons public, 2026 LOCKED; E9.45: betting free, fantasy paid), that means the PAID/GATED data (2026 projections, subscriber tools, the full board) could be lifted straight off the wire, bypassing the UI + the paywall.
⚖️ **THE FREEMIUM SPLIT IS NOW OPERATOR-DECIDED (2026-08-01) — this is the concrete rule E9.56 enforces:** FREE (unauthenticated / non-subscriber) sees **PAST-SEASON model projections + past rankings + past player pages** (the NF3.2 receipts surface — public by design); the entire **2026 (current-season) projection everywhere — rankings, player pages, board, tools — is LOCKED**, and **every locked 2026 data point renders a SUBSCRIBE CTA ("subscribe to unlock")** rather than being blank or absent. ⭐ **THE DESIGN NUANCE THIS CREATES (get it right or you either leak or break the CTA): the anti-scrape rule says the 2026 VALUE must never be on the wire to a non-subscriber; the CTA says the frontend must KNOW a locked 2026 point EXISTS in order to render the prompt. ⇒ a non-subscriber payload carries a per-point LOCKED MARKER (a boolean/placeholder that says "a 2026 value exists here, locked"), NEVER the value itself.** So the split is not "omit 2026" — it's "return `{locked:true}` for 2026, the real number only to an entitled caller." The attacker test (below) must confirm the marker carries NO recoverable 2026 value (no field with the number, no derivable ordering that reconstructs it).
🚨 **THE HONEST REFRAME (state this up front so the session doesn't chase the wrong fix): you CANNOT "mask" an endpoint or its payload from dev-tools — the browser must receive what it renders, so anything fetched is readable + replayable. Obfuscation (renaming/encoding/minifying endpoints) is SECURITY THEATRE — it slows a casual user, a sophisticated one bypasses it in minutes. ⇒ the defense is NOT hiding; it is that THERE IS NOTHING SENSITIVE TO SEE — the server returns ONLY what the caller is ENTITLED to.** Do NOT build endpoint obfuscation.
🔬 DO (the real work): **(1) AUDIT every serving endpoint + every static-JSON payload** the client fetches (`app/backend/` routes + the `fantasy/nfl/*`, `mlb/*`, api-cache S3 blobs) — for each, record: what data it returns, is the gating checked SERVER-SIDE, and does a PUBLIC/non-subscriber response contain any GATED data? **(2) ENFORCE ENTITLEMENT SERVER-SIDE:** gated data (2026 projections, subscriber-only tools, any paid output) is NEVER returned to a non-entitled caller — the endpoint checks the auth token / subscription server-side and FILTERS the response. **(3) SPLIT THE STATIC PAYLOADS BY ENTITLEMENT:** the biggest leak vector — a public static blob that contains gated data. Public blob = the free tier only (e.g. past seasons); the gated tier (2026) served ONLY via an authenticated endpoint that verifies subscription (the NF3.2 requirement, app-wide). **(4) MINIMIZE PAYLOADS** to the fields the UI actually renders (drop internal/model/debug fields — don't ship what isn't displayed). **(5) RATE-LIMIT / BOT-PROTECT** (WAF / API-Gateway throttle / Cloudflare) — the ONE lever that addresses SCRAPING: it won't stop one user reading one payload, but it stops a competitor bulk-pulling the entire public board in one pass; consider server-side pagination/search so the full dataset isn't handed over in a single call.
⚠️ **RUNTIME-GATE — TEST IT AS AN ATTACKER (the only real proof):** as an UNAUTHENTICATED (and as a free-tier) caller, hit the endpoints DIRECTLY (curl/replay, not the UI) and confirm the gated data (2026 projections / subscriber content) is NOT retrievable — a UI that hides it while the payload still carries it FAILS. Do this on the real deployed surface. CI can't prove this; it's a live check.
```

```
PHASE 1 — STAND UP IN PARALLEL (NO cutover): deploy the Dagster OSS services on Railway (use the **Railway MCP** for services/env/redeploys — secrets WRITE-ONLY), point at the Railway PG for Dagster storage, deploy `pipeline/` as the code location, get webserver + daemon HEALTHY, confirm the defs load (15 jobs/9 schedules) **with schedules still OFF.**
PHASE 2 — VALIDATE: manually trigger the key jobs on the self-hosted instance (`predict_today_morning`, `lineup_monitor`, `statcast_catchup`, `write_serving_store`) → confirm output PARITY with Dagster+ (same picks served, same serving-store writes); confirm sensors/schedules fire correctly (test without cutting over); confirm the HALT/WARN/ALERT failure tiers behave.
PHASE 3 — CUTOVER (the critical moment, at a LOW-RISK time — NOT mid-slate): DISABLE all schedules/sensors on Dagster+ → ENABLE on the self-hosted Railway instance. Keep Dagster+ as INSTANT ROLLBACK (re-enable its schedules). Monitor a FULL daily serving cycle end-to-end on self-hosted (morning predict → intraday lineup_monitor → statcast_catchup → write_serving_store).
PHASE 4 — DECOMMISSION: after a clean multi-day window, tear down Dagster+ Serverless (STOP THE BILL); confirm $0 Dagster+ going forward.
Read: `pipeline/` (jobs/ops/sensors/schedules + the `Definitions`) + `services/dbt_runner/` (the Railway deploy pattern to mirror) + the Dagster OSS deploy docs (daemon + webserver + Postgres storage + gRPC code server) + CLAUDE.md failure-contract + the E11.0b/E11.14 Dagster-cost context + `infrastructure/`.
Do: the phased migration; Railway MCP for the infra; operator runs the cutover + the Dagster+ teardown (>1-min / billing steps → operator). MEASURE the new Railway flat compute cost vs the $139 Dagster+ projection → report the net saving.
Gate/AC: self-hosted Dagster (daemon+webserver+code-server+PG) HEALTHY on Railway; all 15 jobs/9 schedules + sensors ported + VALIDATED (parity with Dagster+ on the serving jobs); cutover at a safe time with Dagster+ retained as rollback; a full daily serving cycle verified end-to-end on self-hosted; Dagster+ decommissioned after the clean window; failure-contract tiers intact; net cost saving reported; CI green. **⚠️ NEVER both running schedules at once.**
```

```
▶ Story prompt — E11.13 Python test-suite speedup + structure (600+ tests are taxing CI + every story's ship)   [Infra · Session B · DX · fast-follow]   (2026-06-25, operator)
WHY: the Python suite is 600+ tests across 43 files (`betting_ml/tests` + `scripts/tests`) run SERIALLY with `uv run pytest -v --tb=short` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the Unit Tests CI job) — no parallelism, no slow/fast split, no marker registry (`pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options]` has only testpaths + pythonpath). Every story's pre-handoff gate (CLAUDE.md requires green pytest before handoff) AND the CI job pay the full serial runtime → it's slowing ships.
🔒 NON-NEGOTIABLE — this is a SPEED + STRUCTURE cleanup, NOT a coverage cut. PRESERVE every regression guard (the INC-13, leakage-guard, side-attribution, op-diet, contract-guard tests each catch a REAL shipped bug). Do NOT delete tests to go faster. Remove a test ONLY if it is PROVABLY redundant with a named twin — list the exact (removed, kept) pair in the handoff. Same effective coverage out the other side.
Read: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the Unit Tests job — `uv run pytest -v --tb=short`) + `pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options]` + `betting_ml/tests/` + `scripts/tests/` + CLAUDE.md "CI gates" (targeted-tests-during-dev / full-suite-when-cross-cutting) + the existing "text-based, no Snowflake" guard pattern (e.g. `test_book_odds_leakage_guard.py`).
DO:
 1. PROFILE FIRST: `uv run pytest --durations=50` → the top-25 slow tests (expect a handful to dominate — Snowflake/S3/network IO, heavy model fits, large fixtures). Put the table in the handoff; the cleanup targets THESE, not a blanket rewrite.
 2. PARALLELIZE: add `pytest-xdist`; run CI (and the local gate) with `-n auto` — the single biggest win for an independent-test suite. Fix any test that breaks under parallelism (hidden cross-test state / shared `/tmp` files / global singletons) — that's a real latent bug, not an xdist problem.
 3. FAST/SLOW SPLIT: register a `slow`/`integration` marker in pyproject; mark the heavy/IO offenders; CI runs a FAST gate (`-m "not slow" -n auto`, returns quickly = the per-push handoff gate) + a separate SLOW job (`-m slow`). BOTH required for merge, but the fast gate unblocks ships.
 4. MOCK EXTERNAL IO: convert any test that hits Snowflake/S3/network/real artifacts to mocks or tiny in-repo fixtures (extend the text-based-no-Snowflake pattern) — usually where the seconds hide.
 5. FIXTURE HYGIENE: session/module-scope expensive fixtures rebuilt per-test; lazy-import heavy modules so collection is cheap.
 6. TRIM CI NOISE: drop `-v` in CI (keep `--durations=10` for ongoing visibility).
 7. ANTI-REGRESSION: document the new run commands (fast gate vs full) in CLAUDE.md so future sessions use the fast gate, and keep the marker discipline so the suite can't silently re-bloat.
Gate/AC: effective coverage UNCHANGED (no guard dropped; any removal names its redundant twin); full suite green; **report before/after wall-time** for both the full suite and the fast gate; xdist-safe (no parallel flakes — run it 3× to confirm); markers registered + heavy tests marked; CLAUDE.md updated with the fast-gate command. `uv run pytest` (full) green.
Closeout (per §0.1): END with an ⏭️ Operator handoff — `git add <paths>` (pyproject.toml, ci.yml, conftest/fixtures, any test/marker edits, CLAUDE.md), the before/after timing + the `--durations` table, and confirmation no coverage was lost.
```

```
▶ Story prompt — INC-14 Duplicate `is_current` lineup rows → inflated training-sample weight (investigate + fix)   [Model-A / data-correctness · 🔴 OPEN]   (surfaced by E11.1-W1d, 2026-06-25)
WHY: the W1d session downgraded a `unique_combination_of_columns(game_pk, side)` test on `feature_pregame_lineup_features` (error→warn) to unblock a merge — and it's WARNING, i.e. there ARE duplicate `(game_pk, home_away)` rows. Root-cause hypothesis: `feature_pregame_lineup_state` (SCD-2) has MULTIPLE `is_current=true` rows for the same game+side (the transition failed to flip old rows to `is_current=false`), and `feature_pregame_lineup_features.sql`'s `lineups` CTE (`WHERE is_current=true`) fans them through → the feature store → **inflated sample weight on affected games in the v6 / E2.x / E5.x training matrices.** The guard is now SOFT so this won't self-surface again. Data-correctness, not a serving outage — but it silently biases training.
DO — PHASE 1 (QUANTIFY first, don't fix blind):
 • Run the diagnostic (Snowflake MCP, read-only): `SELECT game_pk, home_away, COUNT(*) cnt FROM feature_pregame_lineup_state WHERE is_current=true GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*)>1 ORDER BY cnt DESC;` → HOW MANY (game×side) keys are duplicated, over WHAT date range (is it recent / all-history / a specific window?), and the dup multiplicity.
 • Trace REACH: do the dupes actually land in `feature_pregame_lineup_features` (and downstream `feature_pregame_game_features` / the training matrix)? Quantify the % of games affected in the train window → that's the inflated-weight magnitude. If it's a handful of games → minor; if systematic → assess whether v6/E2.x/E5.x need a re-fit on de-duped data.
DO — PHASE 2 (FIX the SCD-2 transition, root cause not band-aid):
 • Find where `feature_pregame_lineup_state` is written/updated (the lineup ingest / SCD-2 logic) → ensure EXACTLY ONE `is_current=true` per (game_pk, home_away): the new-lineup write must ATOMICALLY flip the prior current row(s) to `is_current=false` (or use `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game_pk, home_away ORDER BY <effective_ts> DESC)=1` to pick the latest). Add a guard so a future race can't reintroduce dupes.
 • Stopgap if the root-cause fix is involved: dedup in the `lineups` CTE (latest-effective per game×side) so the feature store is clean immediately, then fix the source.
 • RE-PROMOTE the `unique_combination_of_columns(game_pk, side)` test back to `severity: error` once clean (it's a real serving-adjacent correctness guard, not peripheral DQ — the warn downgrade was a temporary unblock).
Gate/AC: dup count quantified + training-reach assessed (with a re-fit recommendation if systematic); SCD-2 transition fixed so exactly one current row per game×side; feature store de-duped; the test back to `error` and PASSING; `uv run pytest -m "not slow"` + `dbtf compile` green. ⚠️ Snowflake reads via MCP, read-only; the long re-derive → operator.
Closeout (per §0.1): operator handoff — the diagnostic result + magnitude, the SCD-2 fix + `git add`, the test re-promotion, and the model-re-fit recommendation (if any).
```

```
▶ Story prompt — E11.16 dbt-Build CI deferral env — stop the `state:modified+` false-failures (the INC-15-class root)   [Infra · CI/CD · 🧭 OPUS · Medium]   (2026-06-25, operator — bundle into W2)
WHY: the `dbt-Build CI` runs `state:modified+` but has **NO prod deferral environment** (404 for project 441385) → partial builds hit missing-UPSTREAM nulls = **FALSE failures** (this was the `has_odds` artifact root + the noise that MASKED tonight's real W1d type break). With a deferral env, `modified+` builds resolve unbuilt upstreams from the PROD manifest instead of building/erroring on them. **AND it's compile-only today** — which is exactly how a runtime type error (the INC-15 W1d break) merged clean. Fix both.
Read: `.github/workflows/dbt_build_ci.yml` + dbt `--defer`/`--state`/`--favor-state` docs + the E11.2-T2 state pattern (`/tmp/dbt-state/`, the prod manifest already uploaded to S3 for `source_status:fresher+`) + the `has_odds` artifact (`feature_pregame_game_features_raw.sql:350`) + CLAUDE.md CI-gates.
DO:
 • Stand up a PROD deferral target: maintain/refresh the prod `manifest.json` (reuse the E11.2-T2 S3 state location) on each prod build, and add `--defer --state <prod-manifest>` (+ `--favor-state` where appropriate) to the CI `state:modified+` build → unbuilt upstreams resolve from PROD, not a partial CI build. No more missing-upstream-null false failures.
 • **RUNTIME, not compile (the INC-15 fix): the dbt-Build CI must actually RUN `dbtf build --select state:modified+` (with deferral), not just `dbtf compile`** — so a compile-clean / runtime-broken change FAILS CI before merge.
Gate/AC: CI runs `state:modified+` with a working prod deferral env (no missing-upstream-null false failures) AND actually BUILDS (runtime, not compile) → verified on a known-good change + a deliberately type-broken one (must FAIL); CI green on a clean change.
Closeout (per §0.1): operator handoff — CI workflow + state-management changes + `git add`; note the deferral-env setup steps.
```

```
▶ Story prompt — E11.9-T2 Convert `feature_pregame_game_features(_raw)` full-CTAS → incremental   [Infra · cost · ⭐ biggest remaining Snowflake lever · 🔒 ML-CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL]   (2026-06-23, E11.9 deferral)
WHY: `feature_pregame_game_features(_raw)` is a full `create or replace` of the ENTIRE history on (nearly) every intraday rebuild (~3,233×/7d; E11.9-A removed only the *redundant* 2nd rebuild). Converting to `incremental` — rebuild only the games whose inputs changed, not all history — is the single biggest remaining Snowflake cut. **BUT this mart FEEDS THE LIVE SERVING PATH (predict_today + the serving store), so a stale/incorrect incremental row = bad predictions → it was deliberately deferred from E11.9 for validation. Get the SCOPE right or don't ship.**
⚠️ THE HARD PART — the incremental scope (read this twice): a scheduled game's features CHANGE through the day as lineups confirm, weather/odds/probable-pitchers land, EB posteriors update. So "rebuild today's game_pks" is NOT enough — you must re-materialize EVERY game whose upstream inputs changed since the last run, or you serve stale features. Safe filter = re-process all games with `game_date >= current_date - N` (N covering late-confirming/retro updates, e.g. 2–3 days) UNION any game whose source rows updated since the last build (ties to E11.2-T2 `source_status` thinking). Under-scope → stale features served (silent, ML-correctness bug). Over-scope → less savings but still correct (prefer this if unsure).
Read: feature_pregame_game_features.sql + feature_pregame_game_features_raw.sql (current materialization + the as-of `< game_date` guards from E1.8) + what TRIGGERS the rebuilds (pipeline/ops intraday + lineup rebuild ops) + the freshness gate that reads `_raw` build epoch (predict_today `_FRESHNESS_STALE_HOURS`) + predict_today.py (the live read) + E12 (the tier-aware serving-parity harness — REUSE it as the gate) + dbt incremental docs (unique_key, incremental_strategy merge vs delete+insert, on_schema_change).
Do:
 (1) Pick the config: `materialized='incremental'`, `unique_key` = the mart's grain (game_pk, or game_pk+side), `incremental_strategy` = `merge` or `delete+insert`, `on_schema_change='sync_all_columns'`; the `is_incremental()` filter = the SAFE scope above (date window UNION changed-source games). Preserve every E1.8 as-of guard (`< game_date`) — incremental must NOT change point-in-time semantics.
 (2) Keep a periodic FULL-REFRESH net (weekly `--full-refresh`, like the daily build) to correct any incremental drift.
 (3) VALIDATE (the gate — operator runs the >1-min dbt builds): build incremental and build full-refresh on the SAME data over a multi-day window → **assert byte-identical per game × per column** (zero diff). Specifically prove NO STALE ROWS: take a game, change an upstream input (lineup/weather), run incremental, confirm that game's features re-materialized. Then run predict_today on both → **identical predictions** (E12 harness green, all tiers). 
 (4) Measure the rebuild-cost drop (WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY COMPUTE_WH vs the 57.57 cr/7d E11.9 baseline + the rebuild query count).
Gate/AC: incremental output == full-refresh (byte-identical over the window); proven no-stale-rows on an upstream change; predict_today predictions UNCHANGED (E12 parity green, all tiers); weekly full-refresh net retained; measured credit/rebuild-count reduction; `uv run pytest` + `dbtf compile` green; changelog = none (infra, predictions must NOT change).
Closeout (per §0.1): the long `dbtf build` validations → operator; ⏭️ Operator handoff — the incremental-vs-full parity evidence + the no-stale-rows proof + the predict_today parity + the credit delta + git add. If parity is NOT perfect, DO NOT ship — revert to full-CTAS and report the diff.
```
