PHASE 2 — MC GAME SIMULATOR: chain the PA model through innings with correct base-out-score state TRANSITIONS (advance runners by outcome) given lineup + starter + a bullpen plan → per-team run distribution → game total / run-diff / NRFI / team-totals. Store params/grid, not raw samples.
PHASE 3 — EVAL: calibrate the run distribution (PIT, CRPS, calib_80) on HELD-OUT games; compare vs E2.1/E2.3 (the incumbent per-side NegBin distribution) for product value, AND vs the DERIVATIVE close (team/alt totals, each vs its own close) at PBO<0.2/DSR>0 for edge. HONEST: a better-calibrated sim is product value (distribution UX, NRFI/team-total projections) even with zero edge — ship that finding either way.
Read: dbt mart_pa_outcome_substrate (E13.12) + E2.1/E2.2/E2.3 (the incumbent totals distribution + the dispersion-calibration recipe) + E13.8 benchmark (the derivative-vs-main-line bar) + betting_ml eval discipline (purged CV/PBO/DSR/CRPS) + the lakehouse_loc/duckdb pattern + (future) E13.10.
SEQUENCING: heavy + multi-session — Phase 0+1 first (PA model is the concrete first deliverable), then 2, then 3; heavy training/sim → operator/runner (>1-min). Cost-gated: confirm headroom before the heavy runs. Gate/AC per phase; ⏭️ operator handoff (run-order + git add + ablation_results); no changelog unless a sim output ships to serving (separate, later, careful).

WHY (operator reframe): every edge result so far (E1.9, E13.1, E13.3) re-permuted the SAME feature mart, which is ~all season/career aggregates + EB posteriors + archetype matchups. E1's "more feats ≠ edge" proved REDUNDANCY WITHIN those axes — it did NOT establish COVERAGE of the axes we lack. You can't model your way to signal that isn't represented. Concrete gap already found: the FanGraphs 7d/14d/30d windows are INGESTED + preserved in stg_fangraphs__hitting_leaderboard but reach ZERO feature; only season-level Stuff+ was ever modeled (the leaky/collapsed one). GOAL (the bar): get the data mart into the BEST possible state so that a null H2H/totals edge result is a TRUSTWORTHY "no edge," not an artifact of missing/incomplete data. Until coverage is demonstrably complete, "no edge" only means "no edge given what we happened to have." This audit makes the conclusion defensible.
Read: dbt/models/staging/fangraphs/* (windowed leaderboard + stuff_plus — what's ingested) + fct_fangraphs_* + feature_pregame_* (what reaches features = season only) + baseball_data_mart_inventory.md + sport_data_platform.md (sources) + E1.1 (purged CV) + E1.4 (PBO/DSR) + E1.8 (the season Stuff+ leak — derived/recency features carry the SAME leak risk) + gtm_strategy §0 (spend discipline — free-first sourcing).
Do:
 (1) INVENTORY: every column across (a) live contracts, (b) marts, (c) ingested-but-UNUSED staging (FanGraphs windows are the first found; look for others), (d) source data available but un-ingested. Classify by signal AXIS.
 (2) GAP-MAP across THREE categories (this is the expansion — not just momentum):
    • **(A) TEMPORAL / recency** — the lead gap: short-window FORM/MOMENTUM (FanGraphs 7/14/30d wRC+/wOBA, Stuff+/velo TREND, team rolling run-scoring & run-prevention, bullpen recent workload/availability). Mechanism: recent form can reflect a REAL change (mechanics/health/role/lineup) the season aggregate masks.
    • **(B) COMBINATORY / derived** — signal we're leaving on the table by NOT engineering interactions/ratios/differentials from columns we ALREADY have, with a BASEBALL-DOMAIN RATIONALE (e.g. lineup wOBA × THIS starter's handedness split = platoon-adjusted matchup; park run-factor × team batted-ball profile; bullpen fatigue × expected game length / times-through-order; pitcher pitch-mix × opponent archetype). ⚠️ Discipline: do NOT blanket-generate all pairwise interactions (curse of dimensionality + the E1 redundancy finding); hypothesis-driven only. Note tree models capture some interactions implicitly → explicit columns matter most for the GLM/linear lane + high-order/sparse interactions trees miss.
    • **(C) EXTERNAL / un-ingested data available online** — run a domain checklist of what a serious MLB modeler uses vs what we have: defensive metrics (OAA/DRS), granular park dimensions/altitude, wind VECTOR relative to park orientation, baserunning, platoon splits, pitcher times-through-order penalty, catcher–pitcher pairing, rest/travel/B2B, day-night, lineup projection-vs-actual, etc. Flag each as have / free-to-add / paid (paid = validate-free-first, gated like F5/E2.0c per spend discipline). Identify the highest-value FREE additions.
 (3) RANK all candidates (A+B+C) by: orthogonality (low corr w/ existing contract features) × plausible market-underweighting × leak-clean availability × build cost. Pre-register each candidate's hypothesis.
 (4) TEST top candidates: leak-clean (STRICTLY < game_date, point-in-time as-of) + SHRINKAGE/regression-to-mean (a 7d spike is mostly variance — isolate persistent change, not noise); INCREMENTAL lift over the v6 contract under purged CV; gate winners on PBO<0.2 + DSR>0.
 (5) Ship only winners — into BOTH the H2H model AND the E2 per-side totals marginals. **🎯 PRIORITIZE the E2.1 per-side run MEANS as the integration target:** E2.2 §4.5 showed the per-side mean barely separates games (between-game mean-var 0.894) AND team scoring form is more autocorrelated than single-game W/L → a recency/derived signal is MOST likely to lift a number there. Totals-means first; H2H second. Drop the rest with the recorded null.
DELIVERABLE = a COMPLETENESS DOSSIER: the inventory + the three-category gap map + per-candidate ruled-in/ruled-out verdict, such that the H2H/totals "no edge" conclusion is defensible (we checked the axes, not just the columns we happened to have). This is the exit criterion the operator asked for.
HONEST EXPECTATION: MLB momentum is weak + markets move on form; combinatory signal is often already implicit in trees; many external sources are priced-in. The edge (if any) is narrow. **But a clean null AFTER a complete-coverage audit is itself the valuable deliverable** — it's what lets us honestly conclude the model track's value is product-quality (calibrated projections/distributions/transparency) + fantasy, not a betting edge. Market-microstructure candidates overlap the killed E13.1 — market-aware, separate gate.
Gate/AC: a coverage inventory + gap map (committed doc) + per-candidate leak-clean incremental-lift verdict (purged CV + PBO/DSR + shrinkage) + winners integrated into the contracts (or a recorded null). CI green.
Closeout (per §0.1): long fits → operator; ⏭️ Operator handoff (the inventory/gap doc + ablation_results per candidate + sub_model_registry/contract updates + git add). Feeds the v6 successor + E2 marginals; if it ships signal, re-run the relevant models (and reconsider E13.2 simulator).

▶ Story prompt — E13.8 Market-accuracy benchmark: year×book line quality (H2H + totals)   [Model-A · situational awareness · advisory/transparency only]   (2026-06-23, operator)
WHY: before we re-open the MLB totals/H2H markets we need to know WHAT WE'RE TARGETING — how accurate the market itself is at setting lines, per bookmaker, per year. That tells us (a) the practical CEILING (the sharpest book's accuracy — the bar a "good" model would have to MATCH, since the H2H edge is dead and the product goal is calibration-parity with the close), (b) the SOFT-BOOK SPREAD (where any residual edge could live), and (c) the YEAR TREND (are books sharpening — E3.0b already found soft books converging toward Pinnacle). FRAME: advisory/transparency, NOT a +EV claim — this is a benchmark report for the operator, not a served feature.
🟢 DON'T REBUILD WHAT EXISTS: `feature_edge_book_market_era_quality.sql` (E3.0b) already computes the core table — grain (book, market_type, season) for book ∈ {pinnacle,bovada,caesars,fanduel}, market ∈ {h2h,totals}, with `closing_brier`, `closing_log_loss`, `mean_vig`, `mean_abs_dist_to_sharp` (vs Pinnacle), all on the leakage-guarded de-vigged CLOSE (snapshot_ts < commence_time). START by querying that mart for the year×book table; only EXTEND from there.
DO — Part A (fast, from the existing mart): build the mart (`dbtf run --select feature_edge_book_market_era_quality`) and emit the year×book table for BOTH markets — closing_brier + log_loss + mean_vig + mean_abs_dist_to_sharp, sorted market→book→season, with n_games. This alone answers the operator's ask.
DO — Part B (extensions, the new value): (1) WIDEN book coverage beyond the 4 canonical books to the full oddsapi book set in `odds_snapshots_historical` (the mart hard-codes 4 in its `where lower(s.bookmaker) in (...)` — generalize it or write a sibling query; keep Pinnacle as the sharp anchor for dist_to_sharp). (2) ADD TOTALS LINE-ACCURACY the Brier doesn't capture: per (book, season) mean `|total_line − actual_total_runs|` (RMSE of the posted line vs realized runs) + PUSH RATE (share where total_runs == line) — "how close is the number" is distinct from "how well-calibrated is the over/under price." (3) ADD H2H favorite hit-rate (share of games the de-vigged favorite won) alongside Brier. (4) ANCHOR with REFERENCE ROWS so the numbers are interpretable: the base-rate/no-skill Brier (H2H ≈ 0.249 from home-win rate; totals ≈ 0.25 from the over rate) and an explicit "Pinnacle = ceiling" callout. Known prior (E13.6): the served market H2H Brier sits ~0.247 (barely beats the 0.249 coin-flip floor) — expect H2H books tightly clustered just under no-skill; totals likely carries more separable structure (that's where the open question is).
Leakage/honesty: everything on the CLOSE, every snapshot already < commence_time (preserve that guard); pushes excluded from Brier (already handled), counted separately for the push-rate metric. No column may assert a +EV bet (honest-framing rule) — this is a benchmark, not a signal.
Read: dbt/models/feature/feature_edge_book_market_era_quality.sql (+ its `_…yml`) + feature_edge_sharp_anchor_backtest.sql (E4.3, adjacent book-quality drift) + mart_game_results + the `american_to_implied_sql` macro + build_roadmap E13.8 row + the E13.6 calibration finding (the H2H ceiling context).
Gate/AC: a committed report `ablation_results/e13_8_market_accuracy_benchmark.md` with the year×book tables for both markets (Part A) + the widened-book + totals-line-accuracy + reference-row extensions (Part B) + a 3–5 sentence "what we're targeting" read (the ceiling, the spread, the trend). If a sibling/generalized dbt model is added, CI green (`dbtf build --select state:modified+` + compile). No changelog (operator-facing analysis, not user-facing).
Closeout (per §0.1): operator handoff (run-order for the dbt build + the query/script, >1-min flagged + git add incl. the report and any model change). Feeds the totals (E2.3 / E13.4 lift-tests) + H2H re-eval as the accuracy bar.

▶ Story prompt — E13.17 "WHEN WOULD WE **NOT** ABSTAIN?" — characterize the abstain rule + find any principled non-abstain regime   [Model · 🧭 OPUS · ⭐ operator-originated 2026-07-20 · follow-on to `best_alpha=0` · NOT a serving bug]   (NEW 2026-07-20, from the E11.20 P0 triage)
🎯 WHY (operator): the daily predict logs show **100% abstain** ("Bovada ML 0 games", 0 totals edges) — verified 2026-07-20 as **STANDING, INTENTIONAL behavior** (`best_alpha=0`), matching the prior 5 days, on the HEALTHIEST feature matrix of the window (imputed 0.7 vs 4.1/6.0/5.3). So this is **not a serving defect** — but "we abstain on literally everything, always" is an unexamined end-state worth characterizing: **under what conditions, if any, WOULD the system not abstain?** Today nobody can answer that precisely, which makes the abstain rule un-auditable and the product story ("we only speak when we have something to say") unquantified.
🔬 DO: (1) **CHARACTERIZE the current rule** — trace exactly what makes a game abstain (the `best_alpha=0` gate + whatever threshold/permission logic remains post-Epic-19-retirement); document the decision path end-to-end. (2) **QUANTIFY the counterfactual** — over history, at what edge/threshold would ANY game clear? Plot the distribution of our model-vs-market disagreement: how far is the closest game from the bar, and is the bar structurally unreachable (i.e. `best_alpha=0` ⇒ abstain-always by construction) or merely rarely-reached? **If it's unreachable by construction, SAY SO plainly** — that's the honest finding and it retires the question. (3) **IF a principled non-abstain regime exists**, it must clear the §0.5 deflated bar (pre-registered, purged CV, PBO<0.2/DSR≥0.95, forward-CLV net of vig) — this is NOT a license to lower the bar until something passes. ⚠️ **THE TRAP: "find a threshold where we'd have bet and won" is pure data-mining** (the E13.9/E13.13 lesson) — the threshold is part of the model, fit in-fold, judged out-of-fold.
🔒 HONEST FRAME: a defensible "we abstain because the market is efficient and we say so" is a PRODUCT asset (the honest-analytics wedge), not a failure. A clean "abstain-always is correct given `best_alpha=0`" is a fully valid deliverable. NO edge claim without the deflated gate.

 2. ⭐ **CONDITIONAL-EDGE / SUBSET-ACCURACY analysis (operator ask — "is a SUBSET of selections actually somewhat accurate, even though the AGGREGATE is null?"):** PRE-REGISTER + test slices — by market, confidence bucket, line range, favorite/dog, home/away, book, game type — for realized CLV/accuracy. ⚠️ under FULL deflation (PBO<0.2/DSR≥0.95/FDR + a PLACEBO control) because slicing IS a multiple-comparisons data-mine (the E5.4/E13.9 trap). ▶ Story prompt — E13.18 CLEAR-UNDERDOG segment-specialist H2H model — does a model SPECIALIZED to lopsided matchups beat the general champion on that segment?   [Model · 🧭 OPUS · 🔬 §0.5 bake-off · liquid-market R&D · `best_alpha=0`]   (NEW 2026-07-29, operator hypothesis)
🎯 WHY (operator hypothesis 2026-07-29): the general v6 H2H champion is trained + selected across ALL matchups; clear-favorite / clear-underdog games are a distinct REGIME (heavy moneylines — the classic favorite-longshot-bias zone) where a single global model may be miscalibrated. HYPOTHESIS: a model SPECIALIZED to games with a clear underdog is better-CALIBRATED on that segment than the general champion. ⭐ **DISTINCT from E13.9's #2** (which tests whether the CURRENT model has conditional edge on the favorite/dog SLICE) — E13.18 builds + tests a SEPARATE model for the segment. If you want to know whether the segment is even interesting first, run E13.9's favorite/dog slice diagnostic as a cheap precursor.
🎯 **DEFINE THE SEGMENT (pre-register — the key design choice):** "clear underdog" = a game where one side's moneyline is beyond a threshold. ⚠️ nearly EVERY non-pick'em H2H game has a `+` side, so "clear" needs a REAL cutoff (e.g. underdog implied-prob ≤ 0.40 and ≤ 0.33, or favorite ML ≤ −180). Pre-register ≥2 thresholds, count BOTH toward deflation, and ⛔ do NOT tune the cutoff on the eval fold.
🔬 DO (§0.5 bake-off — a specialist vs the general FOIL):
 1. **ASSEMBLE once** (SF-free lakehouse → parquet): the H2H feature matrix restricted to clear-underdog games (per each pre-registered threshold) + realized outcome + the market ML (for the honest calibration/CLV read; the MODEL itself stays market-blind — non-market model, `best_alpha=0`).
 2. **BAKE-OFF ≥3 learner classes** for the SPECIALIST (trained ONLY on the segment) + the mandatory FOILS: (a) the incumbent v6 general champion evaluated ON the segment (the null to beat), (b) the general model + a segment/ML-interaction feature (a cheaper alternative to a whole separate model — the direct-learned foil). Pre-register; Optuna-tune each; purged/embargoed CV per serving tier.
 3. **METRIC = CALIBRATION on the segment** (per the §0.5 selection-metric hygiene — for binary H2H use log-loss / Brier + a reliability/PIT read on the underdog win prob, and SANITY-CHECK vs an oracle floor so the metric isn't inverted). The question is "is the specialist better CALIBRATED on lopsided games," NOT "does it win more." Report model-vs-market on the segment honestly — any EDGE claim needs the FULL deflation gate (PBO<0.2 / DSR≥0.95 / FDR + placebo; slicing to a segment IS a multiple-comparisons data-mine → the segment selection COUNTS toward deflation).
 4. **VERDICT:** ship a specialist ONLY if it beats BOTH foils on the segment under the deflated gate. Likely + VALID outcome = the general model already handles the regime (null) → record it. A survivor = a SEGMENT-ROUTED model (route clear-underdog games to the specialist, all others to the champion) — a serving-routing change; SPEC the integration but do NOT wire it unless it clears.
🔒 HONEST FRAME: `best_alpha=0` — a better-calibrated underdog win prob is a CALIBRATION/product improvement, not an edge claim. A SINGLE specialist architecture missing the gate is NOT a trustworthy null (§0.5) — the whole ≥3-learner set + foils, tuned, must fail. ⚠️ small-N: clear-underdog games are a FRACTION of the slate → REPORT THE POWER (ties MH2); an underpowered null ≠ a dead effect. NULL kept NULL.
💾 DATA/CONSTRAINTS: read the v6 H2H feature contract + champion (registry) + the lakehouse H2H training data (DuckDB SF-free); assemble ONCE → parquet (every arm/threshold/fold reads the cache); do NOT `git commit`/`push` (hand back `git add <paths>`); >2-min fits → operator, laptop-vs-box.
GATE/AC: a pre-registered clear-underdog segment definition (≥2 thresholds); a ≥3-learner specialist bake-off vs the general-champion foil + a segment-interaction foil, selected on a CALIBRATION metric under purged CV + full deflation (segment selection counted), power reported; a specialist ships ONLY if it beats both foils deflated (→ spec the segment-routing serving change), else the null is recorded. 🌿 GIT (do this FIRST, before touching any file): `git checkout dev && git pull && git checkout -b <story-branch>`; commit + push to THAT branch, hand back a PR → `dev`. ⛔ NEVER work on / commit to `dev`/`main` directly, ⛔ NEVER `git add -A`; re-check `git branch --show-current` before each commit (a parallel session shares the checkout); any `--publish`/`deploy.sh` is a POST-MERGE operator step. (CLAUDE.md 🌿.) `best_alpha=0`.

⚠️ APP-TARGET GUARD: serving-query side = `scripts/write_serving_store.py`; any UI tweak = `frontend/` ONLY (the Book Comparison lives in `frontend/app/picks/[game_pk]/page.tsx`).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): `_BOOK_ODDS_BATCH` (write_serving_store.py L997) selects the latest COMPLETE snapshot per (event_id, bookmaker_key, market_key) via `MAX(ingestion_ts)` (`complete_snapshots`→`latest_complete`→`latest_odds`) with NO filter on game start. The odds-capture cron keeps ingesting after first pitch → the "latest" snapshot becomes a post-start price → displayed.
FIX: add a PRE-GAME-START leakage guard — restrict `all_odds`/`complete_snapshots` to `ingestion_ts < <game_start>` BEFORE taking MAX, so the served book odds are the latest complete PRE-START snapshot (they FREEZE at the last pre-game price once the game begins). Source the game-start timestamp: commence_time from the odds event / `mart_game_odds_bridge`, or `game_datetime` from `stg_statsapi_games` (join via game_pk). Use the odds event's own commence_time if available (most precise per-event).
SWEEP (mandatory — don't fix only the one surface): audit the OTHER serving odds queries for the same missing guard — the consensus/`mart_odds_consensus`, the EV/edge display path, the game-detail odds blob — anywhere that takes a "latest" odds snapshot for DISPLAY must be `< commence_time`. (The model's edge is computed pre-game upstream in daily_model_predictions; this is about the raw odds DISPLAY surfaces.) List what you checked.
GUARD: add a regression assert / test that no served book-odds row has `ingestion_ts >= commence_time`; QA a known recently-completed game (its Book Comparison shows the pre-game close, not the post-start/settled price).
Read: scripts/write_serving_store.py (`_BOOK_ODDS_BATCH` L997, `_compute_book_odds_payloads` L1191) + mart_odds_outcomes / mart_game_odds_bridge (event↔game_pk + commence_time) + stg_statsapi_games (game_datetime) + frontend/app/picks/[game_pk]/page.tsx (Book Comparison render) + (cross-ref) E9.22 freshness work.
Gate/AC: Book Comparison shows only pre-game-start odds (latest complete snapshot `< commence_time`); the other display surfaces swept + guarded; regression assert added; QA on a completed game; `uv run pytest` + frontend build green. Changelog (user-facing fix).
Closeout (per §0.1): CI green + ⏭️ operator handoff (run-order + git add: write_serving_store.py + any swept query + test + the changelog line) + post-deploy verify (open a live/completed game's pick detail, confirm pre-game odds only).

▶ Story prompt — E9.25 P0 BUG: front-page "Yesterday" pick badge always shows a WIN   [App · frontend + serving · 🔴 P0 TRUST/INTEGRITY · 🔒 NON-NEGOTIABLE transparency]   (2026-06-23, beta-reported)
⚠️ APP-TARGET GUARD (first action): `cat frontend/package.json` → confirm Next.js. UI work is in `frontend/` ONLY (never app/streamlit_*). The serving-query side is `scripts/write_serving_store.py`.
WHY (P0): a beta tester reported the front page shows yesterday's daily pick as a WIN every day — they saw PHI featured + lose, yet "Yesterday" still showed a win. This FABRICATES a winning track record → directly destroys the transparency wedge (gtm §1). Fix immediately + honestly (an honest LOSS shown builds more trust than a fake win).
ROOT CAUSE (two compounding bugs, both confirmed):
 (1) BACKEND cherry-picks a winner — `_FEATURED_YESTERDAY_SERVING_SQL` (scripts/write_serving_store.py ~L888) ends `ORDER BY actual_outcome DESC NULLS LAST ... LIMIT 1`, so among ALL of yesterday's picks it surfaces whichever WON (actual_outcome=1), not the pick that was actually FEATURED. It also qualifies on `qualified_bet = TRUE` while the TODAY query (`_FEATURED_TODAY_SERVING_SQL` ~L830) selects on `layer4_h2h_conviction_flag = TRUE` + earliest `game_datetime ASC LIMIT 1` → the two don't even identify the same pick.
 (2) FRONTEND hardcodes the win badge — `app/page.tsx` renders the "Yesterday" badge as emerald (`bg-[#10b981]`) + `<CheckCircle2/>` UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of `pick.yesterday.outcome` → even a "Loss" string shows green with a ✓.
FIX:
 (a) BACKEND: make "yesterday" track the SAME pick that was featured — reuse the EXACT today-selection logic (the `_FEATURED_TODAY_SERVING_SQL` ranking: conviction-flag qualifier, market-data/post_lineup tiebreak, earliest `game_datetime ASC LIMIT 1`) but for `DATEADD(day,-1,today)`, then LEFT JOIN `mart_clv_labeled_games` for that pick's REAL `actual_outcome`. Remove the `ORDER BY actual_outcome DESC` cherry-pick entirely. Emit an honest outcome status: win / loss / push / pending(actual_outcome NULL = not yet settled). Confirm `actual_outcome` semantics = the BET result for the picked side (team won / over hit), not CLV-positive — if it's CLV-based, use the true game/total result instead (a CLV-positive loss must still read "Loss" to the user).
 (b) FRONTEND: branch the badge on the real outcome — win→emerald + ✓, loss→red + ✗ (e.g. XCircle), push→neutral, pending/unsettled→neutral "Pending" or hide the badge (NEVER default to win). Update the `YesterdayResult` type if a status enum is added.
GUARD: a clean sample where yesterday's featured pick LOST must render red "Loss"; a win renders green; an unsettled game renders pending — verify all three.
Read: scripts/write_serving_store.py (`_FEATURED_TODAY_SERVING_SQL` L830, `_FEATURED_YESTERDAY_SERVING_SQL` L888, the "Build yesterday result" block ~L1808) + frontend/app/page.tsx (YesterdayResult type L25 + the badge render ~L267-280) + mart_clv_labeled_games (actual_outcome definition).
Gate/AC: yesterday's badge reflects the ACTUAL featured pick's REAL result (win/loss/push/pending), selected by the same logic as today; no cherry-pick; frontend badge color/icon/text branch on outcome; QA all three states; `uv run pytest` + frontend build green. **Changelog entry (user-facing fix).**
Closeout (per §0.1): CI green + ⏭️ operator handoff (run-order + git add: write_serving_store.py + app/page.tsx + any type) + the changelog line + what to verify after deploy (load the front page, confirm a known recent loss shows red).

"Dagster goes down" = 3 distinct failure modes → one layer each:
TASKS:
1. **🪦 DAILY-OUTPUT DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH (highest value — do FIRST; outcome-based, catches ALL root causes).** Alert if today's picks aren't in the DynamoDB serving cache (`credence-prod-serving-cache`) by a cutoff (e.g. 8:00am ET). This fires whether the cause was a dead box, a failed dbt build, a bad deploy, or a stuck daemon — it watches the THING USERS SEE, not a process. 2. **📉 BOX / INSTANCE LIVENESS + RESOURCE PRESSURE** — CloudWatch **EC2 status-check alarms** (instance + system reachability) → SNS topic → email subscription (catches instance death / unreachable). Plus resource alarms tuned for this **burstable t4g.medium (2 vCPU, 4 GB, baseline ~40% combined)** — calibrated so normal daily-build/predict bursts DON'T page, only genuine trouble:
   - **🧠 MEMORY/SWAP (highest-value on this box — OOM is the likeliest failure, not CPU):** CloudWatch agent `mem_used_percent` > **85%** for 10 min, AND swap-in-use climbing / `swap_used_percent` > ~50% → alarm.    - **💽 DISK:** root `disk_used_percent` > **85%** (Docker images/logs/parquet temp fill a small root vol).
   - **🔥 CPU — alarm on SUSTAINED, not spikes:** `CPUUtilization` > **90% for 30 min** (3 consecutive 10-min datapoints) → investigate. ⚠️ Do NOT alarm on brief 80–100% spikes — the daily build / `predict_today` / image rebuilds / FanGraphs solves are *expected* minutes-long bursts. At beta volume neither should fire from routine serving; a sustained breach = a runaway process or a heavy retrain mistakenly run on this serving box.
3. **🐳 SERVICE LIVENESS (box up but a container down/daemon not ticking — a plain ping misses this)** — a host-cron healthcheck (~every 5 min) asserting `docker compose ps` all-Up + `curl` dagit:3000 + dbt-runner:8080/health + flaresolverr:8191; on failure publish to SNS/SES. ⛔ Claude does NOT enter credentials / confirm SES identities / subscribe email addresses — the operator confirms the SNS email subscription + any SES sender identity; the prompt specifies WHAT, the operator provisions. CONVENTIONS: do NOT git commit/push (operator); honest framing; >1-min scripts to the operator.

So a Dagster bump = a COORDINATED change across all four + a `dagster instance migrate` against the metadata Postgres, read the release notes for that version, and validate defs load BEFORE the live box. Write this as `services/dagster/aws/UPGRADING.md` (or a runbook section) so the next session doesn't bump one container in isolation.
3. **🤖 Automated update PRs.** Stand up Renovate (preferred) or Dependabot on the repo for the orchestration image tags + Python deps → it raises PRs that flow through the **P5 CI gate** (`dagster definitions validate` + compose-build catches a defs-breaking or unbuildable upgrade BEFORE merge). Group/schedule them (e.g. a weekly batch) so they're not noise; label so app/model deps aren't entangled with orchestration ones.
4. **🔒 Security-patch cadence.** Document a periodic (≈monthly) review: OS `dnf upgrade` on the box (or bake into a fresh AMI/cloud-init — pairs with P5's reproducible box → "replace the box" beats "patch in place"), base-image refresh, and a scan of the Renovate/Dependabot security alerts. Subscribe to Dagster release notes + GitHub security advisories for the pinned components so CVEs surface.
5. **🧪 Test path for upgrades.** An upgrade PR must be green on the P5 CI gate; for a Dagster MINOR/major bump (higher risk), validate on a throwaway/standby box (or the P5 EVENTUAL standby) before promoting to live, and rely on P5 auto-rollback + P6 alerting as the net. Don't promote an un-tested Dagster bump straight to the live daemon.
⛔ Claude does NOT enter credentials / GitHub-app installs — the operator installs Renovate/Dependabot + any registry creds; the prompt specifies WHAT. CONVENTIONS: do NOT git commit/push (operator); >1-min scripts to operator.
AC: all compose image tags pinned (no `:latest`; digests where practical) + Python deps pinned to the lockfile; `UPGRADING.md` documents the Dagster coordinated-bump + `instance migrate` rule; Renovate/Dependabot raising grouped orchestration-dep PRs that pass the P5 CI gate; a documented security-patch cadence + advisory subscriptions; an upgrade test path (CI-green + standby-validate for Dagster bumps). Operator handoff with the Renovate/Dependabot setup steps + the `git add` list (pinned compose, UPGRADING.md, renovate.json/dependabot.yml).

5. **Guardrails** — the dev run must be unable to write prod (verify with a dry-run/IAM scoping); dev box IAM role grants dev-target access only (no prod serving write). Document the env in `aws_resources.md`.

▶ E9.34   ✅ BOTH BUGS FIXED + VERIFIED (Sonnet, 2026-06-28; operator-confirmed post-deploy). 
 • **BUG 1 (EV times +5h) — RENDER layer:** `stg_statsapi_games.game_date` is TIMESTAMP_TZ → Pydantic v2 serializes as `...+00:00` (OFFSET, not `Z`). The prior partial fix's `endsWith("Z")` check missed the offset case → appended Z → invalid `"...+00:00Z"` → browser parsed as LOCAL. Fix: `formatGameTime` now uses the string as-is if it ends in `Z` OR matches `/[+-]\d\d:?\d\d$/`, else appends Z (mirrors game-detail `fmtGameTime`); covers all 3 EV call sites.  • **BUG 2 (ATL@SF stuck pending) — settle filter:** MLB Stats API has TWO terminal codes — `'F'` (Final) and `'O'` (Final/Official, after the official scorer; LATE games are usually `'O'` by the nightly settle run). `_final_scores()` in `settle_user_bets.py` queried `status_code = 'F'` only → `'O'` games invisible → bet stuck pending forever. Fix: `WHERE status_code IN ('F','O')`. TZ hypothesis RULED OUT (settle queries by `game_pk`, not date → UTC day boundaries irrelevant).
 Files: `frontend/app/ev-tracker/page.tsx`, `scripts/settle_user_bets.py`, `changelog.json` (2 entries, `2026-06-22` block). CI: tsc + fast gate 683 + changelog-guard green.

**DuckDB-compat checklist (each verified, W3-main + W4):** `::number`→`::decimal(scale)` (explicit scale or values zero); `dateadd('day',n,d)`→`d + interval 'n days'`; `game_date::date` before any RANGE-window/interval (parquet stores it VARCHAR); a result-cast `(ratio)::numeric` is scale-0 in Snowflake (often DELIBERATELY zeroed) — REPRODUCE it, don't "fix" it; confirm every consumer of a zeroed col reads a different (rolling/std) col; **(W4) FanGraphs/big JSON flatten → set `threads=2` + a `memory_limit` (else OOM); httpfs → raise `http_timeout`; the live `pitcher_clusters` keys on `fit_date` (NOT `snapshot_date`), unique `(pitcher_id, season)`; hash WARNs on FLOAT cols = stringification artifact, not a defect (row-exact + PK-unique is the real gate).** **(W5) `at` is a DuckDB RESERVED word (→`at_`); a CTE named the SAME as its base table self-references in DuckDB (→rename e.g. `team_ref`); the `{% if is_incremental() %}…{% else %}<real where>{% endif %}` else-arm must be HAND-INLINED (the runner's stripper eats it); a literal `{% else %}` inside a SQL `--` comment BREAKS `dbtf compile` ("unknown statement else"); `dbt_utils.date_spine()` can't survive the extractor → inline a DuckDB `range()`; match the retired table's TYPE (`mart_game_results`=DATE, `mart_game_spine`=TIMESTAMP_NTZ — cast `game_date::date`/`::timestamp`); incremental→view = just drop the `incremental` config + the `is_incremental()` WHERE arms (full rebuild). 🐞 **INCREMENTAL TYPE-DRIFT (recurring — INC-15/W1d, INC-16-P0, INC-19 2026-06-29):** when a dual-branch change makes a feature column compute as a DIFFERENT type than the EXISTING Snowflake incremental table (classic: DuckDB FLOAT vs an existing `NUMBER(38,x)`), the incremental run FAILS — `cannot change column … from NUMBER(38,x) to FLOAT` — and HALTs the job. **FIX: manually `DROP` the affected incremental table(s) (+ any downstream model carrying the column) → rebuild fresh** (`--full-refresh` is UNRELIABLE in dbt-fusion — it MERGEs). **PREVENT: CAST the column to a consistent type in the dual-branch model** (DuckDB + Snowflake agree) so the type can't drift. ⚠️ every `feature_pregame_*` incremental model is a W8 candidate for this — cast consistently as you flip each to a DuckDB branch. PARITY-PK: pick the TRUE grain — `mart_home_away_splits` is per-GAME not per-date → PK `(game_pk, team)` (doubleheaders collide on `(team, flag, game_date)`). **(W5b) Snowflake `lateral flatten(input => variant_obj)` → DuckDB list-comprehension unnest (`unnest([{...} for k in json_keys(probs)])`); a direct `cast(... as MAP)` on VARCHAR-JSON FAILS. `matched` is a DuckDB reserved word (MERGE). For Bayesian/k-means TOLERANCE-class migrations: seed-pin (`random_state`), the SEEDED cutover is value-exact (parity row-exact-grade); the ~3rd-decimal band only bites on a DuckDB REBUILD → parity check both paths (drift bands + MAP-cluster agreement ≥98%).** **🧮 BUILDER DUAL-WRITE RULE:** when you migrate a computed-table BUILDER's I/O to `--s3`, that's ADDITIVE if non-migrated consumers (feature layer, deferred marts) still read its Snowflake output → KEEP the Snowflake builder run until those consumers migrate; the builder's Snowflake compute is only ELIMINATED once nothing reads its Snowflake table (track this for the cost AC).
**DISCIPLINE (makes fast safe):** per-mart VALUE-PRESERVING parity BEFORE the view swap (this caught 3 latent serving bugs W1d shipped silently); P6 alerting + the P5 CD auto-rollback are the net. 🚨 **GRANT-PRESERVATION (INC-18, 2026-06-29):** every `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW/TABLE` SILENTLY DROPS Snowflake GRANTs → any object on the request-time fallback path (read by `app/backend/routers/picks.py`/`bets.py`) loses `CREDENCE_API_RO`'s SELECT on recreate → cache-miss 503. INC-18 added schema FUTURE GRANTS + a staging `+post-hook` re-grant in `dbt_project.yml`; **any wave recreating a request-read object MUST confirm its schema has the FUTURE GRANTS (or a post-hook re-grant)** + verify a Snowflake-fallback request returns 200 post-cutover. 🪪 **BOTO3 INSTANCE-ROLE FALLBACK (W7b-1, 2026-06-29 — cost a morning):** on the EC2 box S3 auth is the **instance IAM role** (post-INC-16); `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` is UNSET. **NEVER pass `aws_access_key_id=os.environ.get("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID")` to boto3** — passing `None` DISABLES boto3's default credential chain → `AuthorizationHeaderMalformed`. Pass explicit keys ONLY if present, else fall back to the chain (or use DuckDB `COPY` / a shared `s3_client()` helper). Any NEW boto3 S3 writer must follow this. Mirror/parity-only ops must be **mirror-tier (ALERT-continue), NOT HALT**, until their cutover flag flips. **CUTOVER ORDER (P5 CD live):** build S3 parquet → `parity GREEN` → create the `lakehouse_ext` external tables in Snowflake → THEN commit/PR (merge auto-deploys via CD on `dbt/**`+`scripts/**`) → verify post-deploy. **A precursor (getting a non-mart Snowflake SOURCE into S3) comes before its marts.**
**SEQUENCING:** the mart GROUPS are independent, but every wave edits the SHARED build scripts (`run_w1_lakehouse.py`/`refresh`/the DDL generator) → run **W4→W5→W6→W7 SEQUENTIALLY** (one Opus session each, each builds on the prior's shared-script state) to avoid shared-file merge conflicts. **W7 (readers) is LAST** — it needs every mart it consumes already in S3.

▶ INC-22 — 🔴 P1 SERVING BUG: `write_serving_store_intraday_op` computes TOMORROW's date (UTC-midnight rollover) → evening intraday refresh silently doesn't run   [Serving · 🧭 OPUS · ⭐ ASSIGNED 2026-06-29 as the 3rd parallel session · diagnose-and-fix · parallel-SAFE with W8a + W12]   (2026-06-29, live P1)
🚨 THE BUG (observed 2026-06-29 ~19:12 CDT = 00:12 UTC 6/30): `write_serving_store_intraday_op` resolved **date=2026-06-30** while the live slate is **6/29** → "No predictions for 2026-06-30 — skipping picks/today/featured/ev" + "0 game_pks" + a misleading `ops/heartbeat#daily date=2026-06-30 n_picks=0`. The MORNING op is immune (runs ~13:00 UTC = still 6/29 UTC); only the EVENING intraday ops cross the boundary.

WHY: `healthcheck.sh` paged CRITICAL **4× in 12h** listing `dagster-codeloc`/`-daemon`/`-webserver`/`dbt-runner` "container down" — but the box is healthy (FALSE POSITIVE). Cry-wolf CRITICALs erode trust in the REAL P6 alerts (dead-man switch, the INC-17 model-health alert) → fix the noise.
🥇 **ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed):** the 4 flagged services are EXACTLY the app-image containers the **P5 CD rebuilds** on a `dbt/**`/`scripts/**`/`pipeline/**` merge (`docker compose up -d --build`); `dagster-postgres`/`flaresolverr`/`caddy` (NOT rebuilt) stayed healthy → that's why they're absent from the alert. The 5-min host-cron `healthcheck.sh` step-1 check `docker compose ps --status running --services` lands DURING the recreate window → those 4 are momentarily `restarting`/`created`, not `running` → false "container down". **4 alerts ≈ 4 merges/deploys today** (W3pre, W3-main, E9.34, …), each >1h apart so each clears the 1h cooldown. (NOT the cwd/compose-file gotcha — the script already uses the explicit `-f`.)
FIX (combine, in `services/dagster/aws/healthcheck.sh` + `deploy.sh`):
 1. **Debounce — require ≥2 (ideally 3) CONSECUTIVE failed checks before paging.** Keep a small counter state file (increment on fail, reset to 0 on success); page only when it crosses the threshold. A transient single-check deploy blip won't page; a REAL sustained outage stays failed across checks → still pages (preserve true-positive). This is the robust general fix.
 2. **Deploy-aware suppression:** `deploy.sh` writes a lock (e.g. `/tmp/credence_deploy_in_progress`) at start + removes it in a trap on exit; `healthcheck.sh` SKIPs (or resets the counter, doesn't page) while the lock exists. Directly kills the deploy-window race even if a deploy spans >1 check.
 3. (Optional, sharper liveness) treat `restarting`/`created`/`recreating`/`health: starting` as TRANSIENT (not "down") via `docker inspect` State/Health — only `exited`/`dead`/missing = real down. Step-2's `compose exec … curl` into codeloc also fails mid-recreate → the debounce covers it.
GUARD — don't over-suppress: a genuinely-stopped container (`docker compose stop dagster-daemon` left down across ≥ threshold checks) MUST still page within ~10–15 min.
VERIFY: (a) trigger a real CD deploy (or `up -d --build`) → confirm NO page; (b) stop a core container and leave it → confirm it DOES page after the consecutive-fail threshold; (c) confirm the dead-man switch + other P6 alerts unaffected.

(Small; fold in if scope allows, else flag as a separate P6 follow-on.)
Gate/AC: no false page during a CD deploy (verified on a real deploy); real sustained outage still pages within ~15 min; debounce + deploy-lock in place; ships via P5 CD; `bash -n` clean.
